Definite noun, genitive dual. Object of ilā. Root k-ʿ-b: ankle-bone, knuckle; cube; high status; the Kaʿbah. The dual form specifies both ankles as the limit-point of foot-purification.

Indefinite noun, accusative (predicate of kāna). Root j-n-b: side, flank; to be distant, to avoid, to set aside. Junub = one who is laterally distanced / set apart — traditionally: after sexual contact or seminal emission. The word is morphologically both singular and plural.

Adjective, plural (of marīḍ), pattern faʿlā (broken plural for conditions). Predicate of kuntum. Root m-r-ḍ: to be sick, to be weak, to be unsound. Used for both physical illness and metaphorical disease (of the heart).

Indefinite noun, genitive (governed by ʿalā). Root s-f-r: to uncover, reveal, expose; to travel (because travel exposes one to the open). The traveler is one who is uncovered/exposed — away from the shelter of settled life.

Indefinite noun, nominative (subject of jāʾa). Root '-ḥ-d: one, unique, someone. Here functions as an indefinite pronoun: "anyone of you." The root also yields the divine attribute al-Aḥad (the Absolutely One, 112:1).

Definite noun, genitive. Root gh-w-ṭ: to be low, depressed, sunken. Ghāʾiṭ literally means low-lying terrain / depression in the ground. Used euphemistically for the place of relieving oneself (because people would go to a depression for privacy). Only 2 Quranic occurrences, both in this same legal context (5:6 and 4:43).

Definite noun, accusative (object of lāmastum). Root n-s-w: woman, women; also to delay, to be behind. Nisāʾ = women (as a collective). The definite article marks this as a category, not specific individuals.

Indefinite noun, accusative (object of tajidū). Root m-w-h: water, fluid, liquid. Māʾ is the primary purifying element. Its absence triggers the entire tayammum alternative. The word appears 62 times in the Quran — fundamental to creation, sustenance, and purification.

Indefinite noun, accusative (object of tayammamū). Root ṣ-ʿ-d: to ascend, to rise, to climb. Ṣaʿīd = what has risen/ascended — the surface of the earth, elevated ground, any clean surface that rises from the terrain. Pattern faʿīl (= what undergoes the action, i.e., what has ascended).

Adjective, indefinite accusative. Modifies ṣaʿīdan. Root ṭ-y-b: to be good, pleasant, pure, wholesome. Pattern fayyil (intensive): thoroughly good/pure. The ṣaʿīd must be ṭayyib — not any ground, but clean, wholesome ground.
Noun, genitive plural (governed by بِ) + 2mp possessive pronoun; second occurrence of wujūh in the ayah, now in the tayammum context

Conjunction wa + noun, genitive plural + 2mp possessive. Second occurrence of aydī in the ayah (first was word 10 with washing). Here conjoined with faces as part of the tayammum wiping. Note: the bundle shows no ilā l-marāfiqi limit here — tayammum hands are not bounded to elbows.
Proper noun, nominative (subject of yurīdu). The divine as the subject of intention — what follows reveals the divine purpose behind the purification legislation.

Indefinite noun, genitive (after min). Root ḥ-r-j: to be narrow, tight, constricted; to be in difficulty; to be embarrassed. Ḥaraj = narrowness, difficulty, constraint, discomfort. The divine denies any intent to impose tightness.
Noun, accusative (object of yutimma) + 3ms possessive pronoun. Root n-ʿ-m: to be soft, pleasant, comfortable; to bestow grace; niʿmah = grace, favor, blessing, comfortable provision.
Noun, feminine singular, accusative (direct object of udhkurū). In construct state (iḍāfa) with allāhi. Pattern fi'la — denotes a single instance of blessing.
Proper noun, genitive (muḍāf ilayhi in construct with ni'mata). Establishes divine source of the blessing.

Noun (mīthāq), accusative (second object of udhkurū), with 3rd masculine singular possessive -hu (His). mīthāq is a mīf'āl pattern noun (instrument/means from w-th-q), meaning the instrument of firmness/trust.
Proper noun, accusative (direct object of ittaqū). Second occurrence — here as the object of mindfulness/guarding.
Proper noun, accusative (ism inna). Third occurrence in the ayah — now as subject of the assertion about omniscience.
Adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), fa'īl pattern for intensive/permanent quality. Predicate (khabar) of the inna-clause. Denotes one who possesses knowledge permanently and fully.

Definite feminine plural active participle (ism fāʿil) in accusative (manṣūb) as object (mafʿūl bihi) of ʿamilū. From root ṣ-l-ḥ (to be sound, to restore, to mend). The definite article indicates a known, specific set of deeds. The feminine plural without a head noun implies a substantivized adjective — "the [deeds/things] that are restorative."

Indefinite feminine singular noun (maṣdar/gerund) in nominative (marfūʿ) as delayed subject (mubtadaʾ muʾakhkhar) of the nominal clause. From root gh-f-r (to cover, conceal, protect). Pattern mafʿila indicates the noun of instance or manner. The indefinite form (tanwīn) suggests magnitude — an unquantified, unbounded covering.

Indefinite masculine singular noun (maṣdar/gerund) in nominative (marfūʿ) as second subject of the nominal clause (coordinated with maghfira). From root '-j-r (to hire, to compensate, to reward). The indefinite form (tanwīn) parallels maghfiratun — both are unquantified, indicating boundless magnitude.

Adjective (ṣifa) in nominative (marfūʿ) modifying ajr. From root '-ẓ-m (bone, greatness, magnitude). The faʿīl pattern indicates a permanent, inherent quality — the compensation is inherently immense. Describes the scale of the promised reward.

Definite noun, nominative (AGNT — agent/subject of yurīdu). From sh-t-n: to be remote, to be far from truth/good. Shayṭān = the one who is maximally remote. The definite article specifies THE adversary — a known entity.

Definite abstract noun, accusative (OBJ of yūqiʿa). From ʿ-d-w: to cross over, transgress, be hostile, be an enemy. Al-ʿadāwa = the state of mutual transgression/hostility. NOUN_ABSTRACT form with 6 total occurrences.

Definite abstract noun, accusative (CONJ_N — coordinated object with al-ʿadāwa). From b-gh-ḍ: to hate, to detest, to feel intense aversion. Al-baghḍāʾ = the state of mutual hatred/aversion. 5 total occurrences, all as NOUN_ABSTRACT.

Definite noun, genitive (PREP_OBJ — governed by fī). From kh-m-r: to cover, conceal, veil, ferment. Same word as in 5:90. Here in the genitive after fī, marking the medium through which enmity operates.

Definite noun, genitive (CONJ_N — coordinated with al-khamr after fī). From y-s-r: to be easy, to be facilitated, to draw lots. Al-maysir = gambling, lottery, any game of chance — literally "the instrument of ease" (gaining without effort). 3 total NOUN_CONCRETE occurrences, all as CONJ_N coordinated with khamr.

Gerund/verbal noun, genitive (PREP_OBJ — governed by ʿan). From dh-k-r: to remember, to mention, to be mindful, to invoke. In the construct state with Allāh: dhikr Allāh = remembrance OF Allāh / mindfulness of Allāh.

Proper noun, genitive (GEN_CONS — second term of iḍāfa with dhikr: "remembrance of Allāh"). The divine name. From '-l-h: to be bewildered, to seek refuge, to worship. The name Allāh = the one who is worshipped, the one in whom refuge is sought.

Gerund/verbal noun, genitive (PREP_OBJ — governed by ʿani). From ṣ-l-w: to follow closely, to connect, to pray. Aṣ-ṣalāwa = the formal prayer, the ritual connection. Definite with the article: THE prayer (the established practice).

Active participle, Form VIII (muntafaʿilūna pattern), masculine plural, nominative (PRED — predicate of the nominal question). From n-h-y: to prohibit, to forbid, to reach the end/limit. Form VIII intahā: to cease, to stop, to reach the end, to refrain. Muntahūna = those who are in the state of having desisted.
Proper noun, accusative (manṣūb) as direct object of aṭīʿū. The definite name for the singular divine entity.
Concrete noun, accusative (manṣūb) as direct object of aṭīʿū. Definite with al- (specific messenger). From r-s-l: to send, dispatch. Rasūl = one who is sent, an emissary.
Concrete noun, genitive (majrūr) governed by ʿalā. With possessive pronoun -nā (our). The shift from al-rasūl (word 6) to rasūlinā adds divine possession — the messenger belongs to God.

Abstract noun, nominative (marfūʿ) as subject of the nominal sentence (annamā ʿalā rasūlinā al-balāghu). The verbal noun from balagha (to reach, arrive at). Al-balāgh = the act of delivering a message so it reaches its audience.

Active participle, Form IV (mufʿil), nominative (marfūʿ) as adjective modifying al-balāgh. From b-y-n: to be clear, to separate, to make distinct. Form IV: to make clear, to reveal. Al-mubīn = the one/thing that makes clear.

Noun, active participle feminine plural (definite), genitive case (object of ʿamilū). From ṣ-l-ḥ: to be sound, whole, to repair. The feminine plural with al- generalizes: THE things that restore. First of two occurrences (words 7, 19).
Noun, abstract (indefinite, nominative — subject of laysa). From j-n-ḥ: to incline, to lean to one side, to tilt a wing. Junāḥ = the state of having deviated/inclined toward wrong.
Active participle, feminine plural, definite, genitive. Second occurrence (cf. word 7).
Proper noun, nominative (subject). The divine name. Subject of yuḥibbu.

Active participle, Form IV (mufʿil), masculine plural (accusative — object of yuḥibbu). Definite with al-. Those who bring ḥusn (beauty/goodness) into existence. The ayah ends with the participle form of the verb that climaxes Stage 3 (aḥsanū → muḥsinīn).
Proper noun, nominative (subject/agent of yabluwannakum). The explicit naming of Allāh as agent of the test after the emphatic verb.

Indefinite noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT) in genitive (tanwīn kasra), governed by بِ; shayʾ = thing, something. The indefiniteness creates deliberate vagueness — the test comes through a thing, not named fully yet.

Definite noun, genitive (after min). ṣayd functions as both verbal noun (the act of hunting) and concrete noun (the game animal hunted). Only 6 occurrences in the Quran, all in Surah 5 or closely related contexts.
Noun, feminine plural (aydī = hands) + possessive pronoun -kum (your, plural). Nominative as subject of tanālu. Hands represent the closest range of action — bare-handed capture.

Noun, masculine plural (rimāḥ = spears) + possessive pronoun -kum (your). Nominative, coordinated with aydīkum as subject of tanālu. THIS IS THE ONLY OCCURRENCE of r-m-ḥ in the entire Quran — a hapax legomenon.
Proper noun, nominative (subject of yaʿlama). Second occurrence of Allāh in the ayah — now as agent of knowing rather than testing.

Definite verbal noun (GERUND) in genitive, governed by بِ; al- universalizes — the totality of the unseen. ghayb = the unseen, the absent, the hidden. bi-l-ghayb = in the condition of absence/hiddenness — when no one sees.

Noun, masculine singular, indefinite, nominative (subject of the equational sentence fa-lahu ʿadhābun). The indefiniteness (tanwīn) amplifies: not just any specified punishment but an unspecified one — leaving its nature open.

Adjective (ṣifa), indefinite, nominative (qualifying ʿadhāb). From '-l-m = pain. The pattern faʿīl here functions as an active participle (muʾlim = causing pain), not passive. The punishment itself causes pain — it is an active agent of suffering.

Definite noun (maṣdar used as concrete noun), accusative (OBJ). From ṣ-y-d: to hunt, to catch game. Al-ṣayd = the game animal, or the act of hunting. The definite article makes it generic: all game, not a specific animal. Only 6 occurrences in the Quran — all in Surah 5's iḥrām legislation (5:1, 5:2, 5:94, 5:95, 5:96×2).

Noun (broken plural of ḥarām or ḥarīm), nominative (PRED of the nominal sentence antum ḥurum). From ḥ-r-m: to be forbidden, sacred, inviolable. Ḥurum = those who have entered the state of iḥrām — pilgrims in sacred consecration where certain normally-permitted acts become forbidden. Only 8 occurrences in this specific nominal form (5:1, 5:95, 5:96, + others).

Active participle, Form V (mutafaʿʿil), accusative (CIRCUM = ḥāl). From ʿ-m-d: to support, to prop up, to intend. Form V = reflexive intensive: to direct oneself deliberately toward something. Mutaʿammid = one who acts with deliberate intent. Only 7 occurrences of this root in the Quran; only 2 as mutaʿammid (here and 4:93). Both mark intentional killing.

Noun (maṣdar), indefinite nominative (SUBJ of an implied sentence: "then [there is] a jazāʾ"). From j-z-y: to recompense, to requite, to suffice. Jazāʾ = the proportional return for an action, whether reward or punishment. QIRAAT: (1) fa-jazāʾun mithlu [7, canonical] — jazāʾ nominative with tanwīn, mithlu as adjective; (2) fa-jazāʾu mithli [7, canonical] — jazāʾ in iḍāfa with mithli (genitive), meaning "the recompense OF the equivalent"; (3) fa-jazāʾan mithla [Irreg] — accusative; (4) fa-jazāʾuhu [shawādhdh] — with pronoun suffix.

Noun, nominative (ADJ to jazāʾun in the canonical reading; or genitive as muḍāf ilayhi in the iḍāfa variant). From m-th-l: to resemble, to be like, to compare. Mithlu = the like, the equivalent, the counterpart. This is the calibrating term: the penalty must match the killed animal.

Definite noun, genitive (PREP_OBJ of mina). From n-ʿ-m: to be soft, pleasant, blessed; naʿam = livestock (camels, cattle, sheep, goats). The root spans blessing/softness and domesticated animals. Al-naʿam with the definite article = the category of domestic livestock as a whole. QIRAAT: an-naʿmi [Irreg] — with sukūn on ʿayn (contracted form).

Noun (maṣdar), indefinite genitive (GEN_CONS = muḍāf ilayhi of dhawā). From ʿ-d-l: to be balanced, equal, just; to turn aside. ʿAdl = justice, equity, balance — the quality the two arbiters must possess.

Noun (maṣdar), indefinite accusative (CIRCUM = ḥāl). From h-d-y: to guide, to lead, to present/offer. Hady = a sacrificial animal offered at the Ka'ba — the specific form of the equivalent animal. The root h-d-y spans guidance and offering: what is guided/led to the sanctuary. QIRAAT: hadiyyan [Irreg] — with tashdīd on yāʾ (different morphological form, same meaning).

Active participle, Form I (fāʿil pattern), accusative (ADJ to hadyan). From b-l-gh: to reach, to arrive at, to attain. Bāligh = one that reaches — the offering must physically arrive at the Ka'ba. This is an iḍāfa with al-kaʿba: bāligha l-kaʿbati = "reaching the Ka'ba."

Definite noun, genitive (GEN_CONS = muḍāf ilayhi of bāligha). From k-ʿ-b: cube shape, ankle-joint, prominence. Al-kaʿba = the cubic structure in Mecca, the sacred house. Only 4 occurrences of this root in the Quran (5:6, 5:95, 5:97 + one more). The Ka'ba is named here as the destination of the offering — the sacred geography that anchors the penalty.

Noun, indefinite nominative (CONJ_N = conjoined noun, alternative to jazāʾ). From k-f-r: to cover, conceal, deny. Kaffāra = an act that covers/erases a sin — expiation. The same root that means "to disbelieve" (to cover the truth) here means "to cover a transgression through compensatory action." QIRAAT: (1) kaffāratun ṭaʿāmu [7, canonical] — kaffāra as separate noun, ṭaʿām as badal/apposition; (2) kaffāratu ṭaʿāmi [7, canonical] — iḍāfa construction: "the expiation OF feeding."

Noun, nominative (APPOS = apposition to kaffāratun, or muḍāf ilayhi in the iḍāfa variant). From ṭ-ʿ-m: to taste, to eat, to feed. Ṭaʿām = food, nourishment, feeding. Here it specifies the form of the expiation: feeding the needy.

Noun (intensive adjective, plural of miskīn), genitive (GEN_CONS = muḍāf ilayhi of ṭaʿām). From s-k-n: to be still, to dwell, to settle. Miskīn = one who has become still/immobilized — by poverty, inability, helplessness. The plural masākīn denotes the class of the needy. QIRAAT: miskīnin [Irreg] — singular instead of plural.

Noun (maṣdar), nominative (CONJ_N = conjoined noun, third alternative). Second occurrence of ʿ-d-l in this ayah. Here ʿadl means "equivalent, counterbalance" — not "justice" as a quality but "the proportional match in quantity." QIRAAT: ʿidlu [Irreg] — different voweling (kasra on ʿayn), same meaning.

Noun (maṣdar), accusative (ACC_SPECIF = tamyīz = specification). From ṣ-w-m: to abstain, to refrain, to stand still. Ṣiyām = fasting — specifically abstaining from food, drink, and intercourse from dawn to sunset. The accusative tamyīz specifies: "the equivalent of that, [in the form of] fasting." Only 13 occurrences of this root in the Quran.

Noun (maṣdar), accusative (OBJ of yadhūqa). From w-b-l: to be heavy, to rain heavily, to have grave consequences. Wabāl = heavy consequence, the weight of one's action returning. Only 8 occurrences of this root — 4 as wabāl + amr.

Noun, genitive (GEN_CONS = muḍāf ilayhi of wabāl) + 3rd person masculine singular pronoun suffix -hi. From ʾ-m-r: to command, to order; amr = affair, matter, command. Here amr = the violator's conduct/action — the affair whose consequence he must taste.
Proper noun, nominative (AGNT = agent of ʿafā). First of three occurrences of Allāh in the closing section.
Proper noun, nominative (AGNT of yantaqimu). Second occurrence of Allāh in the closing — now as the agent of retribution, not pardon.
Proper noun, nominative (SUBJ of the nominal sentence). Third occurrence of Allāh — now as the subject of a declarative statement of attributes.

Adjective (qualitative), indefinite nominative (PRED of the nominal sentence). From ʿ-z-z: to be rare, mighty, powerful, inaccessible. ʿAzīz = the one who cannot be overcome — might as inaccessibility. Often paired with ḥakīm (wise); here paired with dhū ntiqām (possessor of retribution).

Noun (Form VIII maṣdar), genitive (GEN_CONS of dhū). From n-q-m: to take vengeance. Intiqām = the act of exacting retribution. This is the verbal noun of the same root as yantaqimu (word 51) — closing the ayah by naming the attribute that was just enacted.

Gerund (verbal noun), nominative (PASS_SUBJ — passive subject of uḥilla). From ṣ-y-d: to hunt, catch, pursue. As a gerund, ṣayd can mean the act of hunting OR the thing hunted (catch/game). This ambiguity is significant: does uḥilla apply to the activity or the product?
Definite noun, genitive (GEN_CONS — in iḍāfa with ṣayd). From b-ḥ-r: to be wide, vast; to split open. Al-baḥr = the sea, any large body of water.
Noun, nominative (CONJ_N — coordinated with ṣayd as second subject of uḥilla). With possessive pronoun هُ referring to al-baḥr (the sea). From ṭ-ʿ-m: to taste, eat, feed. Ṭaʿām = food, nourishment.

Gerund, accusative (PURP — purpose/reason accusative or ḥāl). From m-t-ʿ: to enjoy, benefit from, provision. Matāʿ = provision, temporary enjoyment, usufruct. The accusative signals purpose: made lawful AS provision.

Definite noun (NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), genitive (governed by li); faaala intensive/habitual active participle pattern from s-y-r; sayyara = those who travel habitually/intensively; the only Quranic occurrence of this form as NOUN_ACTIVE_PART in PREP_OBJ role

Gerund (verbal noun), nominative (PASS_SUBJ — passive subject of ḥurrima). Same root and form as word 3, but now in the prohibition clause. The repetition of ṣayd in both clauses creates structural symmetry: ṣaydu l-baḥr (lawful) vs ṣaydu l-barr (forbidden).
Definite noun, genitive (GEN_CONS — in iḍāfa with ṣayd). From b-r-r: to be righteous, faithful, open; al-barr = dry land, open ground; also: the righteous one, the faithful one.

Noun, accusative (V_COP_PRED — copulative predicate after dumtum: "you remained ḥurum"). From ḥ-r-m: same root as ḥurrima (word 12). Ḥurum is the plural of ḥarām or ḥarīm — those in a state of iḥrām (pilgrim sanctity).
Proper noun, accusative (OBJ of ittaqū). The supreme name, al-ilāh contracted to Allāh. Object of taqwā: the one toward whom one directs protective consciousness.
Proper noun, nominative (marfūʿ) as agent (fāʿil) of jaʿala. Root '-l-h: divinity, godhood, the object of worship.

Noun, accusative (manṣūb) as first object (mafʿūl bih) of jaʿala. From root k-ʿ-b: cube, ankle-bone, anything protruding or elevated. The word al-kaʿba appears only twice in the entire Quran (5:95 and 5:97), both in Surah al-Māʾida.
Noun, accusative as apposition (badal) to al-kaʿba. Root b-y-t: to spend the night, to shelter; bayt = house, dwelling, shelter; also a line of poetry.

Noun (functioning as adjective), accusative in agreement with al-bayt. Root ḥ-r-m: to forbid, prohibit; to be sacred, inviolable; to be deprived. MASAQ tags as NOUN_PROP, functioning as adjective (ADJ role).

Gerund (maṣdar), accusative as second object (mafʿūl bih thānī) or ḥāl of al-kaʿba under jaʿala. Root q-w-m: to stand, rise, maintain, sustain. The form qiyām is the gerund of qāma. Qira'at variants exist: qiyaman, qiwāman, qawāman, qayyiman.

Prepositional phrase: PREP لِ (lām al-ikhtiṣāṣ, designating beneficiary) + definite noun النَّاسِ in genitive; al- universalizes scope to all humanity; the preposition marks the beneficiary of the divine arrangement (qiyāman li-n-nāsi)
Noun, accusative as conjoined object (maʿṭūf) of jaʿala. Root sh-h-r: to make visible, to publicize, to draw (a sword); shahr = month (the period marked by the visible new moon).

Same root and form as word 5. Accusative adjective modifying ash-shahra. Second occurrence of al-ḥarām in this ayah — first modifying al-bayt, second modifying ash-shahr. The repetition links spatial and temporal sacrality.

Noun, accusative as conjoined object of jaʿala. Root h-d-y: to guide, to show the way; hady = offering animal (literally: what is guided to its destination, i.e., guided to the sanctuary for sacrifice).

Noun, accusative as conjoined object of jaʿala. Root q-l-d: to twist, to hang around the neck, to encircle; qilāda = necklace; qalāʾid = garlands hung around the necks of sacrificial animals to mark them as offerings. Also: maqālīd = keys (that which is hung/twisted on a ring). Only 4 total Quranic occurrences of this root.
Proper noun, accusative as ism anna (subject of anna-clause). Second occurrence of Allāh in the ayah.
Noun, genitive (majrūr) after fī. Plural of samāʾ. Root s-m-w: to be high, to rise, to be elevated. As-samāwāt = the heavens, the elevated realms, the upper dimensions.
Noun, genitive after fī. Root '-r-ḍ: earth, ground, land. The pairing as-samāwāt wa-l-arḍ encompasses all of created existence.
Proper noun, accusative as ism anna. Third occurrence of Allāh in the ayah.

Prepositional phrase: PREP بِ (bāʾ al-taʿdiya, making ʿalīm transitive toward its object-domain) + noun كُلِّ in genitive; in iḍāfa with shayʾin; together bi-kulli shayʾin specifies the unrestricted scope of divine knowledge
Noun, genitive in iḍāfa with kull. Root sh-y-ʾ: to will, to want; shayʾ = a thing, an entity, anything that exists or can be willed into existence.

Adjective (qualitative intensive form, faʿīl pattern), nominative as predicate (khabar anna). Root ʿ-l-m. The faʿīl pattern intensifies: not merely ʿālim (a knower) but ʿalīm (intensively, deeply, comprehensively knowing). Third occurrence of ʿ-l-m in this ayah.
Proper noun, accusative (subject of anna, put in accusative by anna's governance). The divine name.
Qualitative adjective (faʿīl pattern), nominative as predicate of anna-clause (khabar anna). In iḍāfa (construct state) with al-ʿiqāb — the tanwīn is dropped due to iḍāfa.
Gerund (maṣdar), genitive in iḍāfa with shadīdu. From ʿ-q-b: heel, to follow on the heel, consequence, aftermath. The al- makes it definite — THE retribution, the known consequential follow-through.
Proper noun, accusative (subject of second anna-clause). Second occurrence in the ayah — the divine name is deliberately repeated rather than replaced by a pronoun.

Intensive adjective (faʿūl pattern), nominative as predicate of second anna-clause (khabar anna). The tanwīn (ٌ) marks it as indefinite and unbound — unlike shadīdu which is in iḍāfa. Paired with raḥīm as dual predicate.

Intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern), nominative as second predicate of the anna-clause (khabar thānī). Paired with ghafūr — the two predicates accumulate: Allāh is [covering-over] AND [womb-merciful]. The shaddah on the rāʾ is assimilation from the preceding tanwīn of ghafūrun.

Definite noun, genitive case (majrūr by ʿalā). From r-s-l: to send, to dispatch. Rasūl = one who is sent, a messenger. The definite article indicates a specific, known messenger. Genitive follows the preposition ʿalā.

Definite abstract noun, nominative case (marfūʿ) — mubtadaʾ muʾakhkhar (delayed subject) in the ḥaṣr construction. The definite article signals THE conveyance — not any conveyance, but the specific act of delivering the divine message. From b-l-gh: to reach, to arrive, to attain maturity.

Proper noun, nominative case (marfūʿ) — mubtadaʾ (subject) of the nominal sentence. The name Allah derives from '-l-h: to worship, to be bewildered, to seek refuge. Fronted before the verb yaʿlamu, creating a nominal sentence that emphasizes the identity of the knower.
Definite adjective used substantively (as noun), nominative case — subject of yastawī. The al- makes it categorical: the foul-as-a-class.
Definite adjective used substantively, nominative case — second subject of yastawī coordinated by wa. The al- makes it categorical.
Gerund (maṣdar), nominative case — subject of aʿjabaka. Construct state (iḍāfa) with al-khabīthi. The abundance itself is what does the impressing.
Definite adjective in genitive case — second term of iḍāfa with kathra. Repeats word 4 (al-khabīthu) but now in genitive: the foul AS POSSESSED BY abundance.
Proper noun, accusative case — direct object of ittaqū. The one through/against whom the shielding operates.
Noun, masculine plural (irregular: no singular from this form). Vocative case (called by yā). Construct state with al-albāb.
Noun, abstract, genitive case — second term of iḍāfa with ulī. Plural of lubb: the core, the kernel (of a nut), the essence, the innermost part. Metaphorically: pure intellect.

Noun, abstract/concrete, plural of shayʾ (thing). Indefinite accusative (but ashyāʾ is a diptote — takes fatḥa for genitive after ʿan). The indefiniteness is significant: unspecified things, not particular things.
Noun, concrete/proper, definite with al-. Subject of yunazzalu (passive subject = the thing being sent down). From q-r-': to read, to recite, to gather.
Proper noun, nominative (subject of ʿafā). The divine name — agent of pardoning.
Proper noun, nominative. Subject of the nominal clause (wa-llāhu ghafūrun ḥalīm). The repetition of Allāh (words 22 and 25) frames the closing: Allāh pardoned (ʿafā) → Allāh is ghafūr ḥalīm.

Adjective, intensive form (faʿūl), indefinite nominative. Predicate of the nominal clause. From gh-f-r: to cover, to conceal, to forgive. The faʿūl pattern indicates intensiveness — one who covers extensively and repeatedly.

Adjective, qualitative (faʿīl), indefinite nominative. Second predicate of the nominal clause. From h-l-m: to be forbearing, to exercise patience, to withhold reaction. Describes deliberate restraint — not inability to punish but choice not to.
indefinite noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), nominative (AGNT), masculine singular used collectively
active participle (NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), masculine plural accusative, form I (fāʿilīn pattern), predicate of aṣbaḥū
proper noun (NOUN_PROP), nominative (marfū') as agent (fā'il) of ja'ala; the divine name as subject of the negated verb — God is identified as NOT the source of these categories

concrete noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), indefinite genitive (majrūr by wa-lā extending min); active participle pattern fā'ilah from sāba/yasību — "one that flows/roams freely"; a she-camel set loose to graze freely, consecrated to idols and exempt from use

concrete noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), indefinite genitive (majrūr); fa'īlah pattern from waṣala — "one that connects/joins"; a ewe that bore twins (male and female) — the male would be dedicated to idols because it was "connected" to the female in birth

concrete noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), indefinite genitive (majrūr); fā'il active participle pattern from ḥamā/yaḥmī — "one that protects/guards"; a stallion that sired a set number of offspring and was then freed from riding or burden — his back was "protected"
proper noun (NOUN_PROP), genitive (majrūr by 'alā); God as the target of fabrication — the lies are attributed TO God; same divine name as word 3 but now in different syntactic role
gerund/verbal noun (GERUND), accusative (manṣūb) as direct object of yaftarūna; definite article al- = THE lie, not any lie — the specific, known falsehood of attributing fabricated categories to God
comparative adjective (ADJ_COMP), nominative as subject (mubtada') of the nominal sentence; af'alu pattern = "the more/most of them"; with attached pronoun -hum referring back to alladhīna kafarū

Noun-verb-like form (NOUN_VERB_LIKE), functioning as an imperative — come! From root ʿ-l-w (to be high, elevated). Originally meaning ascend/come up, frozen into an invitation formula. 8 Quranic occurrences as command verb.
Proper noun (NOUN_PROP), nominative case (ḍamma). Subject of anzala. The divine name — agent of revelation.

Definite noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), genitive case (governed by ilā). From root r-s-l: to send, dispatch. Al-rasūl = the one who is sent, the envoy/messenger. Definite article indicates a specific, known messenger.

Gerund/maṣdar (GERUND), functioning as predicate in a nominal sentence. From root ḥ-s-b: to reckon, count, deem sufficient. ḥasbu-nā = our sufficiency, what suffices us. With attached 1st person plural pronoun.

Concrete noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), accusative case (object of wajadnā), with 1st person plural possessive pronoun -nā. From root '-b-w: to be a father. Plural of ab (father). Used for ancestors broadly, not only direct parents.

Compound interrogative-concessive particle: hamza (interrogative) + wa (conjunction) + law (conditional). Introduces a rhetorical question with concessive force: would they still say this even if...? The hamza makes it interrogative; law makes it hypothetical.
Concrete noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), nominative case (subject of kāna). With 3rd person masculine plural possessive pronoun -hum. Second occurrence of ābāʾ in the ayah — now shifted to third person.

Abstract noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT), accusative case (object of yaʿlamūna). Indefinite and nakira — anything at all. From root sh-y-ʾ: to will, to wish; shayʾ = a thing, anything. In the accusative after lā yaʿlamūna, it creates absolute negation: they know nothing-at-all.
Noun, plural of nafs, accusative + 2nd person masculine plural pronoun -kum. Functions as the object of the quasi-imperative ʿalaykum. The accusative case confirms ʿalaykum's verbal force.
Proper noun, genitive (governed by ilā). The divine name, etymologically from '-l-h (to be bewildered, to seek refuge, to worship).

Noun (mīm-maṣdar, ism makān), nominative (subject). From r-j-ʿ: the place or act of returning. + 2nd person masculine plural pronoun -kum. Functions as the subject of the nominal sentence (ilā llāhi marjiʿukum).

Noun (ism maṣdar/adjective), accusative (ḥāl = circumstantial). From j-m-ʿ: togetherness, gathering, collectivity. The tanwīn accusative functions as ḥāl — describing the state in which the return occurs: all together.
Verbal noun (gerund), nominative as subject of the sentence (predicate is ithnān). From sh-h-d: to be present, to witness, to testify.
Noun of place/time in genitive (iḍāfa to -kum). Establishes the spatial-social scope of the testimony.
Noun, accusative as object of ḥaḍara. With attached pronoun -kum (your, plural).
Verbal noun (gerund), nominative as agent (fāʿil) of ḥaḍara. Death is the grammatical subject that acts upon the person.
Noun (abstract), genitive in iḍāfa with ḥīna. From w-s-y: to enjoin, to charge, to bequeath.
Numeral noun, nominative as predicate (khabar) of shahādatu. The core legal requirement: two witnesses.
Verbal noun (gerund), genitive in iḍāfa with dhawā. From ʿ-d-l: to be just, balanced, equitable.
Comparative adjective, dual nominative. From '-kh-r: otherness, being last/different.
Abstract noun, genitive after min. With pronoun -kum. Marks the external community.
Concrete noun, genitive after fī. The territory through which one travels.
Active participle noun (feminine), nominative as agent of aṣābat. Same root as the verb — cognate.
Gerund, genitive in iḍāfa with muṣība. Second occurrence of m-w-t in this ayah.
Abstract noun, genitive after min. Temporal: after the prayer.
Gerund, genitive in iḍāfa with baʿd. The ritual prayer as temporal marker for the oath.
Proper noun, genitive after bi. The divine name invoked as oath-guarantor.
Abstract noun, accusative as object of nashtarī. The worldly gain one might accept for false testimony.
Abstract noun, genitive in iḍāfa with dhā. The kinship that might tempt witness-corruption.
Gerund, accusative as object of naktumu. Second occurrence of sh-h-d in this ayah.
Proper noun, genitive in iḍāfa with shahāda. God as owner of the testimony.
Active participle, masculine plural, genitive after min. Those who carry ithm (sin, guilt).

Definite gerund/masdar in genitive (governed by بِ); from sh-h-d "to witness, be present"; al- particularizes — THE specific testimony required in this legal case
Noun, genitive (governed by ʿalā), with attached possessive pronoun hā (referring to al-shahāda, feminine). From w-j-h. Wajh = face, countenance, direction, aspect, manner, front.
Noun, nominative (passive subject of turadda), indefinite with tanwīn. Plural of yamīn. The indefiniteness is significant: some oaths, unspecified oaths — any oaths from the replacement witnesses.
Noun, genitive (governed by baʿda as muḍāf ilayhi), definite through possessive pronoun -him (their, referring to the original witnesses). Same root as word 12 but now definite and possessed.
Proper noun, accusative (direct object of ittaqū). The divine name. Object of the imperative: be conscious of Allāh specifically.
Proper noun, nominative (subject of lā yahdī). The divine name. Now the subject of the declarative sentence — God as the agent who does not guide.
Noun, accusative (direct object of yahdī), definite. From q-w-m. Qawm = a people, a group who stand together, a collective.
Active participle, masculine plural, accusative (adjective/qualifier of al-qawma). Definite. From f-s-q. The active participle indicates an ongoing state: those who ARE in a state of fisq.
Proper noun, nominative (marfūʿ) — subject (fāʿil) of yajmaʿu. The definite name of the divine, with the alif-lām as intrinsic to the proper noun, not a definite article.
Noun, definite, accusative (manṣūb) — direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of yajmaʿu. Plural of rasūl (one who is sent). The definite article al- indicates all the messengers, not a subset.
Noun (gerund/maṣdar), accusative because governed by lā (nafyi l-jins). From ʿ-l-m: to know, to mark, to distinguish. The negated gerund creates an absolute: zero knowledge.

Intensive adjective (ṣīghat mubālagha) on the faʿʿāl pattern. Indicates extreme degree or habitual/intensive action. More intensive than ʿalīm — not just knowing but exhaustively, comprehensively, persistently knowing. Nominative as predicate (khabar) of inna.

Noun, definite, genitive (majrūr) as second term of iḍāfa (ʿallāmu l-ghuyūbi). Plural of ghayb (that which is hidden/absent). The plural is significant — not one hidden realm but multiple hidden dimensions.

Definite noun (nisba/relative form), accusative/genitive (majrūr by ʾilā). From h-w-r: to return, to be intensely white, to argue/discuss. The ḥawāriyy form is a nisba adjective used as a noun — literally "one associated with ḥawar (whiteness/purity)." Appears 5 times in the Quran, all in connection with Jesus.
Definite noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), genitive (governed by بِ), construct state with 1st person singular possessive pronoun -ī; rasūl = one sent on a mission

Nominal (active participle), Form IV, masculine plural nominative. From s-l-m: to be safe, to be sound, to be whole; Form IV aslama: to submit, to surrender, to hand over. muslimūn = those who are in an active state of submission/surrender. Predicative complement of ʾannanā: "that we are muslimūna." This is the climax of the disciples' response — they escalate beyond the commanded āminū (believe) to declare islām (submission).
Definite relative noun, masculine nominative plural. Subject of qāla. From root h-w-r which carries meanings of whiteness, purity, returning, and intimate dialogue.
Foreign proper noun, vocative case (mansūb due to vocative of muḍāf). The name ʿĪsā appears 25 times in the Quran, always with contextual significance.
Concrete noun, accusative case (apposition to ʿĪsā in vocative construction). Accusative because ʿĪsā is muḍāf (in construct with ibn Maryam).
Foreign proper noun, genitive case (in construct with ibn). Appears 34 times in the Quran — the only woman named by personal name.
Concrete noun with 2nd person masculine singular possessive pronoun, nominative case (subject of yastaṭīʿu). Rabb: lord, master, sustainer, nourisher, educator.

Concrete noun, indefinite accusative (direct object of yunazzila). From root m-y-d. The word māʾida is the active participle of māda/tamīdu (to sway, to tilt, to provide food), giving the table an inherently dynamic quality.
Concrete noun, definite genitive (governed by min). From s-m-w: height, elevation, that which is above.
Proper noun, accusative case (object of ittaqū). The essential divine name.

Active participle, Form IV, masculine plural accusative (predicate of kuntum in the conditional clause). From '-m-n: security, trust, faithfulness. The muʾmin is actively in a state of making-secure/trusting.

Noun, broken plural of qalb, nominative case (subject of taṭma'inna), with 1st person plural possessive pronoun -nā. From q-l-b: to turn, to flip, to invert. The heart (qalb) is so named because it constantly turns/changes states.

Definite active participle, masculine plural, genitive case (majrūr by min). From sh-h-d: to witness, to be present, to testify, to attest. The definite article indicates a known category: the witnesses — a recognized class of people who bear testimony.
Proper noun, foreign (non-Arabic origin). Subject of qāla. The name appears 25 times in the Quran, always with the patronymic ibn/ibna Maryam.
Noun, masculine singular, nominative (muḍāf). Appositive to ʿĪsā, forming the patronymic ʿĪsā bnu Maryam.
Proper noun, foreign (non-Arabic origin), genitive (muḍāf ilayhi in iḍāfa with ibnu). Appears 34 times in the Quran — the only woman named by personal name.
Vocative form of Allāh. The suffix -humma replaces the vocative particle yā. Unique vocative construction — appears 5 times in the Quran in VOC role.
Noun, masculine singular, accusative (vocative/munādā), with 1st person plural possessive pronoun -nā. From r-b-b: to nurture, to raise, to be master of.

Noun, feminine singular indefinite, accusative (object of anzil). From m-y-d: to sway, to tilt, to be unsteady. A māʾida is a table laden with food — semantically linked to swaying/tilting under the weight of provisions.
Noun, feminine singular, genitive (governed by min). From s-m-w: to be high, elevated, lofty. Al-samāʾ is the definite form — THE sky/heaven.
Noun, masculine singular indefinite, accusative (predicate of takūnu). From ʿ-w-d: to return, to come back, to repeat. A ʿīd is etymologically a recurring event — something that returns.
Adjective awwal (first, foremost), masculine singular, genitive (governed by لِ), in iḍāfa with 1st person plural pronoun -nā ("of us"); from '-w-l "to return to the origin/beginning"
Noun, masculine singular, genitive (coordinated with awwalinā via wa), with 1st person plural pronoun -nā. From '-kh-r: to be last, to come after, to be behind.
Noun, feminine singular indefinite, accusative (second predicate of takūnu, coordinated with ʿīdan). From '-y-y: to appear, to be evident.
Adjective, comparative/superlative (afʿal pattern), masculine singular, nominative (predicate). From kh-y-r: good, goodness, well-being, virtue.
Active participle, masculine plural, genitive (muḍāf ilayhi in iḍāfa with khayr). From r-z-q: to provide. Al-rāziqīn = the ones who provide — definite, indicating the class of all providers.

Proper noun (ism ʿalam), nominative case (marfūʿ) as subject (fāʿil) of qāla. The definite divine name. Here functions as the explicit subject of the speech act, establishing that the following words are direct divine utterance.

Active participle (ism fāʿil) of Form II nazzala, nominative as predicate (khabar) of inna. The -hā pronoun suffix refers to the table (al-māʾida, feminine). munazzil = the one who sends down (Form II = intensive/causative). As active participle with inna, expresses imminent certain action ("I am about to send it down" / "I am the one sending it down").

Abstract noun (ism maṣdar/noun of abstract), indefinite accusative (manṣūb). Functions as cognate accusative (mafʿūl muṭlaq) — uʿadhdhibuhū ʿadhāban = "I punish him a punishing." The tanwīn signals indefiniteness, which here amplifies: "a punishment [so great that it defies description]."

Numerical noun (ism ʿadad), indefinite accusative (manṣūb) as direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of uʿadhdhibuhū. aḥad = one, anyone, a single person. In negative context (lā uʿadhdhibuhū aḥadan), it becomes universal: "not a single one" = no one at all.

Abstract noun, definite with al-, genitive plural (majrūr by min). ʿālam = world, realm, domain; al-ʿālamīna = all the worlds, all categories of beings. The sound masculine plural form (-īna) is used uniquely for ʿālam (normally reserved for rational beings), which some grammarians explain by treating each "world" as a community of rational beings.

Proper noun (ism ʿalam), nominative case (marfūʿ) as subject (fāʿil) of qāla. The divine name. From '-l-h: the root encompasses divinity, worship, devotion, bewilderment (lāha = to be bewildered, to seek refuge).

Proper noun, foreign origin (ism ʿalam ajnabī), vocative case. The Quranic name for Jesus. Appears 25 times in the Quran, always with the patronymic "son of Mary" (ibn Maryam). The root '-y-s in Arabic carries meanings of whiteness, fair complexion.

Noun (ism), accusative case (manṣūb) as adjective/apposition to ʿīsā in the vocative. From b-n-y: to build, to construct. Ibn = son, one who is built/produced from. The accusative case follows the vocative of ʿīsā.

Proper noun, foreign origin, genitive construct (muḍāf ilayhi after ibna). The mother of Jesus. Appears 34 times in the Quran. The only woman named by personal name in the Quran. The name is of Semitic origin.
Prepositional phrase: preposition لِ (li, indicating direction/recipient of speech) + definite noun النَّاسِ in genitive; marks the addressees of the alleged command — "did you say TO THE PEOPLE"
Noun with 1st person possessive suffix, accusative (coordinated object). From '-m-m: mother, origin, source, foundation. Umm = mother — the one who is the origin and source.

Noun, accusative dual (manṣūb, muthannā). From '-l-h: deity, object of worship. The dual form ilāhayni = exactly two deities. This is the second object complement (mafʿūl bihi thānī) of ittakhidhū — "take me and my mother AS two gods."

Abstract noun, genitive (majrūr by min). From d-w-n: lowness, inferiority, being beneath. Dūn = below, short of, besides. In min dūni llāhi = "besides/other than Allah" — the standard expression for false worship.
Proper noun, genitive case (majrūr, muḍāf ilayhi after dūni). The divine name in the genitive, completing the compound preposition min dūni llāhi = "besides Allah."

Verbal noun (maṣdar), accusative as cognate accusative (mafʿūl muṭlaq), with 2nd person possessive suffix. From s-b-h: to swim, to float, to glide, to be far from imperfection. Subḥān = the declaration of God's transcendence and freedom from all deficiency.

Prepositional phrase functioning as predicate (khabar) of laysa: بِ (bā' al-zā'ida reinforcing negation) + حَقٍّ (gerund, indefinite genitive) — "what is not for me by [any] right"; the bā' strengthens the negation of laysa — Jesus possesses absolutely no right-claim to the alleged utterance

Abstract noun with 1st person possessive suffix, genitive (majrūr by fī). From n-f-s: self, soul, breath, appetite, essence. Nafs = the innermost reality of a being. Here: "what is in my self" — the hidden interior that God alone accesses.

Abstract noun with 2nd person masculine singular possessive suffix, genitive (majrūr by fī). "Your self" — addressing God. The attribution of nafs to God is a significant theological datum: God has a nafs (self/essence) that is acknowledged as real but inaccessible.

Intensive adjective (ṣīghat mubālagha), pattern faʿʿāl. Nominative as predicate (khabar inna). From '-l-m: to know. The faʿʿāl pattern indicates extreme intensity and exhaustiveness of the quality — not merely "knower" (ʿālim) but "one who knows excessively, exhaustively, intensively."

Abstract noun, definite plural, genitive (muḍāf ilayhi after ʿallāmu). From gh-y-b: to be absent, to be hidden, to disappear. Ghuyūb = plural of ghayb = all the hidden things, all unseen realities. The definite plural encompasses ALL hidden dimensions.
Proper noun, accusative (object of ʿbudū). The definite divine name — the direct object of worship.
Noun, genitive (apposition to Allāh). 1st person possessive yāʾ. Root r-b-b: to rear, nurture, sustain.
Noun, genitive (coordinated with rabbī). 2nd person masculine plural possessive kum. Same root r-b-b.
Noun (faʿīl pattern), indefinite accusative — predicate of kuntu. Root sh-h-d: witness, be present, testify, martyr. Indefinite and time-bounded.
Adjective (faʿīl pattern), definite, accusative (predicate of kunta). Root r-q-b: to watch, guard, observe the neck. Only 3 ADJ_QUALIT in V_COP_PRED. A divine attribute.
Noun, genitive (governed by ʿalā). First element of iḍāfa. Root k-l-l: totality, entirety.
Noun, genitive (iḍāfa with kulli). Root sh-y-ʾ: to will, emerge. A shayʾ is what has willed/emerged into being.
Noun (faʿīl pattern), nominative indefinite — predicate of nominal sentence. Second shahīd in this ayah, now nominative and permanent divine attribute.

Noun (abstract), indefinite, genitive case (kasra + tanwīn). Muḍāf ilayhi governed by kull. The indefiniteness with kull creates universal quantification: every single thing.

Noun, masculine singular, indefinite genitive (object of fī). Quadriliteral root. One of the rarest nouns in the Quran (COUNT: 2, both in 6:7 and 6:91). Possibly a loanword from Greek χάρτης (khartēs) or Latin charta.
Noun, feminine plural of يَد (yad), genitive (object of bi-), with 3rd masculine plural possessive -him. Broken plural أَيْدٍ (aydin). COUNT: 107 (very common).

Verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund), masculine singular, indefinite nominative (predicate, khabar). The predicate of the restriction formula: this is nothing but siḥr. COUNT: 63 (common root). The indefinite form adds dismissiveness — not "THE magic" but "mere magic."

Active participle, Form IV (mufʿil pattern), masculine singular, indefinite nominative. Adjective modifying siḥr. From b-y-n (to be clear, separate, distinct). Form IV = to make clear, to clarify. Definite noun, masculine broken plural of ḥimār, accusative (conjoined object). Root ḥ-m-r. Broken plural pattern faʿīl→fuʿul (ḥumur) or faʿīl (ḥamīr). COUNT=6 in Quran (5 NOUN_CONCRETE, 1 ADJ_QUALIT). The definite article marks the species.

Definite noun, masculine singular (collective), accusative (conjoined direct object). Root z-y-t. The form zaytūn is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) — refers to the species, not a single olive. Second item in the plant catalogue. The definite article marks the category.

Definite noun, masculine singular (collective), accusative (conjoined direct object). Root n-kh-l. Pattern faʿīl — collective noun for the species. Third item in the plant catalogue. The nakhīl is the quintessential Arabian tree, appearing 20 times in the Quran.

Definite noun, masculine plural (broken plural afʿāl pattern), accusative (conjoined direct object). Root ʿ-n-b. The broken plural aʿnāb from singular ʿinab. Fourth and final named item in the plant catalogue. Grapes carry associations with wine — the most culturally loaded item in the list.

Noun (ism), masculine singular, genitive (majrūr by min). Root k-l-l. Functions as a universal quantifier. In construct state (iḍāfa) with thamarāt. The genitive case is governed by the preceding preposition min.

Definite noun, feminine plural, genitive (muḍāf ilayhi in construct with kull). Root th-m-r. Sound feminine plural (-āt). The definite article marks the category. Encompasses all fruit-bearing produce, not limited to the four named items.

Indefinite noun, feminine singular, accusative (ism inna — subject of inna in accusative). Root ʾ-y-y. The indefinite form (āyatan, not al-āya) with lām al-tawkīd creates a specific rhetorical effect: "surely A sign" — indefinite implies one among many possible signs, while the emphasis asserts its reality.

Indefinite noun, masculine singular (collective), genitive (majrūr by li). Root q-w-m. The indefinite form suggests any people who meet the following criterion (yatafakkarūn), not a specific historical group. In construct relationship with the following relative clause.

Definite noun, masculine singular, accusative (mafʿūl bih — direct object of sakhkhara). The definite article marks the category (jins): night as a phenomenon, not one particular night. First of four objects.
Definite noun, masculine singular, accusative (conjoined direct object). Root n-h-r. The definite article marks the category (jins). Second object in the four-item list.

Definite noun, feminine singular, accusative (conjoined direct object). Root sh-m-s. Third object of sakhkhara. The definite article marks the category (jins). Paired with al-qamar as the luminous dyad.
Definite noun, masculine singular, accusative (conjoined direct object). Root q-m-r. Fourth and final object of sakhkhara. Paired with ash-shams.

Definite noun, masculine plural, nominative (mubtadaʾ in nominal sentence, standard reading). Root n-j-m. COUNT: 13 (uncommon — rare root survey required). The nominative case in the standard reading marks it as subject of a new sentence; variants read accusative.

Passive participle, feminine plural, nominative (khabar/predicate in nominal sentence). Form II pattern mufaʿʿal. Echoes the active verb sakhkhara from word 2 — the active divine act restated as a persistent state. The feminine plural agrees with nujūm (broken plural treated as feminine).
Gerund/maṣdar, masculine singular, genitive (majrūr by bāʾ). Root ʾ-m-r. Possessive pronoun -hī refers to God. Semantically rich: amr can mean command, affair, matter, or thing.

Noun, feminine plural, genitive (ism inna in delayed position, genitive by proximity to li- or by lām al-ibtidāʾ construction). Root ʾ-y-y. Indefinite — the tanwīn + indefiniteness under inna suggests abundance (signs too numerous to specify). COUNT: 382 (very common).
Noun, masculine singular (collective), genitive (majrūr by li). Root q-w-m. Indefinite — the tanwīn marks an unspecified people, qualified by the following verb. COUNT: 660 (very common).

Definite noun, masculine singular, accusative (direct object of sakhkhara). Root b-ḥ-r. The definite article is for genus (jins) — the sea as a category, not one specific body of water. Accusative as mafʿūl bihi.

Indefinite noun, masculine singular, accusative (direct object of taʾkulū). Root l-ḥ-m. The indefinite form (tankīr) here indicates the type/kind rather than a specific piece. COUNT: 12, all NOUN_CONCRETE — the root appears only as a noun in the Quran.

Indefinite adjective, masculine singular, accusative (ṣifa modifying laḥman). Root ṭ-r-w. RARE: COUNT 2, both ADJ_QUALIT. The other occurrence is 35:12. The yāʾ tashdīd reflects the wāw→yāʾ shift in the nisba-like pattern.

Indefinite noun, feminine singular, accusative (direct object of tastakhrijū). Root ḥ-l-y. Pattern fiʿla. Indefinite for type (tankīr li-l-nawʿ). The root also yields verbal forms meaning "to adorn, to be sweet" — polysemous range.

Definite noun, accusative (direct object of tarā). Root f-l-k. The word fulk is identical in singular and plural (a collective noun). COUNT: 25, all NOUN_CONCRETE. The definite article is generic (jins). Frequently co-occurs with b-ḥ-r (9 times).

Noun, plural, accusative (ḥāl — circumstantial modifier of al-fulk: "the ships [in the state of] plowing"). Root m-kh-r. RARE: COUNT 2, both NOUN_CONCRETE. The other occurrence is 35:12. Pattern mafāʿil (plural of active participle-like noun). Functions as ḥāl describing the ships' motion.

Gerund (maṣdar), masculine, genitive (governed by min). Root f-ḍ-l + 3ms pronoun -hī (referring to Allāh). Very common root: 104 occurrences. The genitive construction min faḍlihī = "from His bounty" is formulaic in the Quran.

Definite noun, masculine singular, genitive (majrūr by bi). Root n-j-m. The definite article is for genus (al-jinsiyya) — "the star" = stars as a class, not one specific star. Classical: najm can mean star, plant that rises without a stem, or anything that appears/emerges.

Noun, feminine singular (tāʾ marbūṭa), accusative (direct object of taʿuddū). Construct state (muḍāf) — "blessing OF Allāh." The singular form niʿma here functions as a collective/generic noun (ism jins), denoting the entire category of divine blessing rather than one specific favor.
Proper noun, genitive (majrūr by iḍāfa — second term of construct with niʿmata). The genitive case marks Allāh as the possessor/source of the blessing.
Proper noun, accusative (manṣūb — subject of inna, which governs accusative). Second occurrence of Allāh in the ayah, now as the entity whose attributes are being declared.

Intensive adjective (ṣīghat mubālagha), pattern faʿūl. Predicate (khabar) of inna. Nominative (marfūʿ). The faʿūl pattern indicates habitual, intensive, or inherent quality — not a one-time act but a permanent attribute. Tanwīn marks indefiniteness — the attribute is unbound, without limit.

Intensive adjective (ṣīghat mubālagha), pattern faʿīl. Second predicate (khabar thānī) of inna, coordinate with ghafūr. Nominative. The initial rāʾ carries shadda (assimilation from the tanwīn of ghafūr). faʿīl pattern = deep, inherent quality.

Proper noun, nominative (mubtadaʾ — subject of nominal clause). The lām is solar, assimilating the definite article. Functions as the topic of a topic-comment construction with yaʿlamu as the comment.

Noun functioning as quasi-preposition (ẓarf), genitive (majrūr by min). Root d-w-n carries the sense of inferiority, lower status, or being apart from. In min dūni llāhi, it marks the space "below" or "other than" God — a hierarchical exclusion. Occurs 143 times in Quran, almost always in this formula.

Proper noun, genitive (majrūr by iḍāfa to dūn). The divine name Allāh. Root ʾ-l-h relates to worship, divinity. The genitive completes the hierarchical phrase min dūni llāhi: the entities exist "below/besides Allāh."

Indefinite noun, accusative (mafʿūl bih — direct object of yakhluqūna). Root sh-y-ʾ. The indefinite under negation functions as a universal quantifier: "not any thing" = nothing whatsoever. The tanwīn reinforces indefiniteness. 283 Quranic occurrences, always as noun.

Noun of time (ẓarf zamān), genitive (governed by min). Root b-ʿ-d: distance, remoteness. As a temporal noun: "after" = at a temporal distance from. The genitive construct with īmānihī: "after his faith."

Gerund (maṣdar), genitive (muḍāf ilayh of baʿdi), with 3ms pronoun suffix -hī. Form IV verbal noun of '-m-n. The root carries safety, trust, security. The hāʾ pronoun refers back to man (whoever) — "his faith/trust."

Noun, concrete, nominative (mubtadaʾ of the ḥāl clause), with 3ms pronoun suffix -hū. Root q-l-b: to turn over, to flip, to reverse. The heart (qalb) is named for its turning nature — it flips between states. Nominative as subject of the circumstantial clause.

Active participle (ism fāʿil), nominative (predicate/khabar of the ḥāl clause). Quadriliteral root ṭ-m-ʾ-n. Form I of a quadriliteral: iṭmaʾanna (to be at rest). The active participle describes an ongoing state of tranquility. The tanwīn marks indefiniteness — "one who is at rest."

Gerund (maṣdar), genitive (governed by bi-), definite (al-). Form IV verbal noun. The definite article here is for ʿahd (known reference) — THE faith, i.e., the specific faith previously established (īmānihī in word 7). Genitive case governed by the preposition bi-.

Gerund (maṣdar), genitive (governed by bi-), definite (al-). Root k-f-r. The definite article marks the concept as known/established — THE disbelief (the same act named in kafara, word 2). Verbal noun: the act of covering/denying.

Noun, concrete, accusative indefinite (tamyīz — accusative of specification). Root ṣ-d-r: to go forth, to issue from; the chest as the place from which things issue. The indefinite accusative functions as tamyīz: "opened, with respect to chest" — specifying which part was opened.

Gerund (maṣdar), nominative indefinite (mubtadaʾ muʾakhkhar — delayed subject in the predicate-first construction ʿalayhim ghaḍab). Root gh-ḍ-b: to be angry, to be wrathful. The indefinite tanwīn gives the wrath a quality of magnitude — "a wrath" rather than "the wrath."

Proper noun, genitive (governed by min). Second occurrence of the divine name in the ayah. Here marks the source of wrath — contrasting with word 4 where the divine name marks the object of disbelief.

Noun, abstract, nominative indefinite (mubtadaʾ muʾakhkhar — delayed subject). Root ʿ-dh-b: paradoxically yields both ʿadhāb (punishment/torment) and ʿadhb (sweet, fresh water). The indefinite form "a punishment" parallels "a wrath" (word 25) — magnifying through unspecifiability.

Adjective, qualitative (ṣifa), nominative indefinite (modifying ʿadhābun). Root ʿ-ẓ-m: to be great, to be mighty. The adjective intensifies the punishment — not merely punishment but ʿaẓīm (of great magnitude). Pattern faʿīl (intensive adjective).

Gerund (maṣdar), definite, feminine singular, accusative (direct object of istaḥabbū). Root ḥ-y-y. Pattern faʿāla. The tāʾ marbūṭa is part of the root-pattern, not a feminine marker per se. Definite article indicates the generic concept of life.

Noun abstract (functioning as adjective to al-ḥayāt), definite, feminine singular, accusative. Elative/superlative form (fuʿlā) from d-n-w meaning "nearer/nearest" or "lower/lowest." Grammatically an adjective modifying al-ḥayāt.

Active participle pattern (fāʿila), definite, feminine singular, genitive (governed by ʿalā). Root '-kh-r. Functions as a noun (originally adjective: "the latter [life/abode]"). The feminine form matches the elided noun ḥayāt or dār.
Proper noun, definite, accusative (ism anna — subject of anna placed in accusative). Root '-l-h. The lām is assimilated (shamsī). Functions as the subject of the clause "Allāh does not guide..."
Concrete noun, definite, masculine plural, accusative (direct object of yahdī). Root q-w-m. Pattern faʿl. The definite article + following adjective (al-kāfirīn) specifies which people.

Active participle (ism fāʿil), definite, masculine plural, accusative (adjective modifying al-qawm in naʿt construction, matching case). Root k-f-r. Pattern fāʿil + sound masculine plural -īn. The alif after kāf is written with a superscript alif (alif khanjariyya).

noun, concrete, genitive (majrūr by ʿalā), masculine plural with 3mp possessive pronoun -him
verbal noun (gerund/maṣdar), genitive (conjoined to qulūbihim), singular form with 3mp possessive pronoun
noun, abstract (broken plural of baṣar), genitive (conjoined to preceding), with 3mp possessive pronoun
active participle, masculine plural, nominative, definite with al-, predicate (khabar) of ʾulāʾika

active participle used as noun (ism fāʿil functioning as ism), feminine singular, genitive (majrūr) after fī, with definite article al-
active participle (ism fāʿil), masculine plural, nominative (marfūʿ) as khabar of anna (predicate), with definite article al-
Noun, masculine singular, accusative (ism inna), in construct with 2ms pronoun -ka. Root r-b-b. First of two occurrences in this ayah — identical form, but different syntactic positions.
Noun, masculine singular, genitive (majrūr by min), in construct with mā. Root b-ʿ-d. First of two occurrences in this ayah — here baʿdi mā (after what = after) and later baʿdihā (after it).

Noun, masculine singular, accusative (ism inna), in construct with 2ms pronoun -ka. Second occurrence (see word 3). Same form, but now subject of the predicate la-ghafūrun raḥīm rather than predicated with li-lladhīna.

Noun, masculine singular, genitive (majrūr by min), with 3fs pronoun -hā. Root b-ʿ-d. Second occurrence of baʿd (see word 8). The pronoun -hā is ambiguous: may refer to fitna (feminine), hijra (feminine), or the entire sequence of events (treated as feminine collective).

Intensive adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha / pattern faʿūl), nominative as khabar inna. Root gh-f-r. The faʿūl pattern indicates habitual, permanent quality — not a single act of forgiveness but an inherent attribute.
Intensive adjective (pattern faʿīl), nominative as second khabar inna. Root r-ḥ-m. The faʿīl pattern indicates permanent quality. Often paired with ghafūr as a divine attribute couplet.

Noun of totality, nominative (subject of taʾtī). In iḍāfa (construct) with nafsin. Kullu + indefinite singular = distributive: "each individual soul." The nominative marks it as the agent. 377 of 411 Quranic occurrences are NOUN_ABSTRACT — kull functions almost exclusively as a quantifier.

Noun, indefinite, genitive (muḍāf ilayh — second element of iḍāfa with kullu). Root n-f-s spans self/soul/breath/appetite. The indefinite form under kull creates distributive force. First of three occurrences of n-f-s in this ayah (words 4, 7, 11).

Noun + attached feminine singular pronoun -hā, genitive (object of preposition ʿan). Second occurrence of n-f-s. The pronoun refers back to kullu nafsin — each soul argues for its own self. The reflexive construction (nafs + pronoun referring to the same subject) emphasizes self-interest: each soul is its own client.

Noun of totality, nominative (nāʾib al-fāʿil — deputy subject in passive construction). Second occurrence. In iḍāfa with nafsin. Repetition of kullu nafsin from word 3 — the universality is restated for the recompense clause, ensuring no exception.
Noun, indefinite, genitive (muḍāf ilayh). Third occurrence of n-f-s. This nafs is the subject-of-passive (nāʾib al-fāʿil through the iḍāfa chain with kullu): the soul that is repaid.
Proper noun, nominative (agent/subject of ḍaraba). Definite. The subject of both ḍaraba (word 2) and adhāqa (word 21).
Indefinite noun, accusative (direct object of ḍaraba). Pattern faʿal. The indefiniteness signals a new, not-yet-known example is being introduced. qaryatan (word 5) stands in apposition.

Indefinite noun, feminine singular, accusative (apposition to mathalan). Root q-r-y. Only occurs as NOUN_CONCRETE in the Quran (57 times). The indefiniteness marks it as a non-specific exemplar — any town fitting this pattern.

Active participle (NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), feminine singular indefinite, accusative (predicate of kānat). Root ʾ-m-n. Pattern fāʿila. The active participle indicates an ongoing state of being secure, not a momentary condition.

Active participle (NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), feminine singular indefinite, accusative (second predicate of kānat). Quadriliteral root ṭ-m-ʾ-n. Pattern mufʿaʿill from Form I (iṭmaʾanna). The doubled nūn + hamza create a phonetically heavy form mirroring the meaning of settled stability.
Gerund (GERUND), masculine singular, nominative (subject of yaʾtīhā). Root r-z-q. The possessive pronoun -hā links the provision specifically to the town.

Gerund (GERUND), indefinite accusative. Root r-gh-d. Functions as a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) or as a maṣdar describing the manner of the provision's arrival. Rare root: only 3 Quranic occurrences.
Abstract noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT), genitive (governed by min). Root k-l-l. Universal quantifier — "every" place without exception. The genitive construction kulli makānin = "every place."
Noun of time/place (NOUN_TIME_PLACE), indefinite genitive (governed by kulli). Root k-w-n. Pattern mafʿāl — a place where being (kawn) occurs. The indefiniteness under kull creates universal scope.

Abstract noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT), genitive (governed by bi-). Root n-ʿ-m. Plural form anʿum (pattern afʿul) — an intensive or paucal plural of niʿma. This plural form is rare; the more common plurals are niʿam and niʿām.
Proper noun, genitive (iḍāfa — possessive construct with anʿum). Second occurrence of Allāh in the ayah. Here as the source-possessor of the blessings.
Proper noun, nominative (subject of adhāqa). Third occurrence of Allāh in the ayah. Explicitly named as the agent of punishment — not left implicit.

Concrete noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), accusative (second object of adhāqa — double-accusative construction: made-it-taste + the-garment). Root l-b-s. The genitive construction libāsa l-jūʿi = "garment of hunger."

Gerund (GERUND), definite, genitive (muḍāf ilayhi — possessed in construct with libāsa). Root j-w-ʿ. Rare root: only 5 Quranic occurrences. The definite article marks this as THE hunger — categorical, not incidental.
Gerund (GERUND), definite, genitive (conjoined with al-jūʿi in the construct). Root kh-w-f. Paired with hunger to form the complete "garment" of punishment. The definite article = categorical fear.

Indefinite noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), masculine singular, nominative (fāʿil — subject of jāʾa). Pattern faʿūl from r-s-l. The indefiniteness (tankīr) here may serve tafkhīm (aggrandizement) or may indicate non-specificity — "a messenger" rather than "the messenger." COUNT: 513, NOUN_CONCRETE: 333.

Definite noun (GERUND), masculine singular, nominative (fāʿil — subject of akhadha). Root ʿ-dh-b. The definite article marks this as THE punishment — known, expected, previously warned about. COUNT: 373, GERUND: 91. The root carries the famous polarity: ʿadhāb (torment) vs ʿadhb (sweet, fresh water).

Active participle (NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), masculine plural, nominative (khabar — predicate of hum). Root ẓ-l-m. The active participle indicates an ONGOING state — they were continually in the condition of ẓulm at the moment of seizure. Not a one-time act but a persistent condition. COUNT: 315, NOUN_ACTIVE_PART: 137 — the most common form of this root.

Verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund) in the accusative as a cognate accusative (mafʿūl muṭlaq), functioning as an exclamatory declaration. From Form I: sabaḥa. The accusative ending -a is permanent (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf indeclinable in this usage). Governs the following genitive via iḍāfa-like construction.
Noun ʿabd in genitive (governed by بِ) + 3rd person masculine singular possessive pronoun -hi (His); construct phrase establishing exclusive ownership/relationship with God
Noun of place (ism makān) from s-j-d, in the genitive case governed by min. Pattern maf'il = place where the action occurs. Here modified by the following adjective al-ḥarām.
Adjective in the genitive case, modifying al-masjid. Pattern fa'āl indicating an intensive or permanent quality. Functions as the qualifying epithet that specifies which masjid.
Noun of place (ism makān) from s-j-d, genitive governed by ilā. Second occurrence in the ayah, now qualified by al-aqṣā instead of al-ḥarām. Same morphological form as word 7.
Elative/comparative adjective (ism tafḍīl) from q-ṣ-w, in the genitive case modifying al-masjid. Pattern af'al = the most X. Here: the most qaṣiyy (distant, remote, far-reaching).

Feminine plural noun āyāt in the genitive governed by min, with 1st person plural possessive suffix -nā (Our). Pattern fāʿilāt. Broad semantic range: signs, evidences, communications, miracles, verses.
Intensive adjective (ṣīghat mubālagha) on pattern faʿīl, in the nominative as predicate of inna. Denotes one who hears absolutely and completely. Definite with al- marking uniqueness.
Intensive adjective (ṣīghat mubālagha) on pattern faʿīl, in the nominative as second predicate of inna (coordinated with as-samīʿ). Denotes one who sees absolutely and completely. Definite with al-.

noun, genitive (after min), with 1st person singular possessive suffix -ī
indefinite noun/adjective (ADJ_QUALIT), accusative, second object of tattakhidhū

Accusative noun (manṣūb). Functions as either: (a) vocative (munādā manṣūb), (b) apposition (badal) to Banī Isrāʾīl implied in 17:2, or (c) direct object of an elided verb. The word ذُرِّيَّة is etymologically debated — from ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r, to scatter) or ذ-ر-أ (dh-r-ʾ, to create/propagate). Its morphological pattern (fuʿʿīla) is unusual.

Proper noun, foreign origin (ism ʿalam ajnabī), genitive (majrūr) governed by مَعَ. The name نُوح is diptote in Arabic but receives tanwīn here due to the genitive governance. Appears 43 times in the Quran across 28 surahs.

Indefinite accusative noun (nakirah manṣūb). Predicate (khabar) of كَانَ. The pattern faʿl (monosyllabic) — the simplest noun form, suggesting the most fundamental characterization. Indefiniteness emphasizes quality over identity: "a servant" not "the servant."

Indefinite accusative adjective (ṣifa manṣūba) modifying عَبْدًا. The pattern faʿūl is an intensive/exaggerative form (ṣīghat al-mubālagha) — not merely shākir (thankful) but shakūr (one who exhausts gratitude, who gives thanks beyond measure). Functions as second predicate of كَانَ or adjective of عَبْدًا.
