Comparative adjective (ism tafḍīl) used as a substantive noun, masculine plural accusative (manṣūb as direct object of azlafnā). Definite with al- (the). Root '-kh-r denotes lateness, otherness, posteriority. The plural ākhirīna here functions as "the other group" — contextually Pharaoh's pursuing army, defined in opposition to Moses' people who were saved (26:65).

Proper noun, foreign origin (NOUN_PROP_FOREIGN). Accusative (direct object of anjaynā) but indeclinable (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) due to foreign origin and proper-noun status. The name appears ~136 times in the Quran — the most frequently named prophet. Etymologically linked to Egyptian ms/msy ("child/born of") or Hebrew mōsheh ("drawn out [of water]").

Noun of emphasis (tawkīd maʿnawī) in the accusative masculine plural (-īna). Pattern afʿal (elative/emphatic). Functions as tawkīd (corroborative emphasis) for the implied pronoun in man maʿahū or for the entire object phrase (mūsā wa-man maʿahū). Reinforces that the rescue was total — no one in the group was left behind. Classical grammarians classify ajmaʿīna among the special tawkīd words (ajmaʿ, jamīʿ, kulluhum).

Noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT), accusative case (manṣūb) as direct object of utlu. Indefinite in form but definite by genitive construct (iḍāfa) with Ibrāhīm. From root n-b-ʾ. The word nabaʾ in classical Arabic denotes news of great consequence — distinguished from khabar (ordinary news) by its gravity and significance.

Proper noun (NOUN_PROP), genitive (majrūr) in construct with nabaʾa (iḍāfa). Foreign (non-Arabic) name, diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) — declined with fatḥa in genitive position instead of kasra. The name appears 69 times in the Quran. Root b-r-h-m assigned by MASAQ for indexing; the name is conventionally treated as non-derivable from Arabic roots.

Noun (ism), masculine singular (collective), genitive (majrūr, coordinated with abīhi under li-). Root q-w-m denotes standing, rising, establishing. Qawm = a group that "stands together" — a community defined by shared stance, origin, or purpose. The pronoun -hi refers to Abraham. The qawm here are the idol-worshipping people of Abraham's community.

Noun, accusative indefinite (tanwīn). Direct object of naʿbudu. Plural of ṣanam. The indefinite form (not al-aṣnām) may suggest generic/categorical reference — "idols" as a class, not specific named idols. Rare root: only 5 Quranic occurrences, all as NOUN_CONCRETE.

Active participle, masculine plural, accusative (predicate of naẓallu). Form I participle of ʿakafa. Functions as the predicate complement of the copular verb naẓallu — "we remain ʿākifīna." The -īna ending marks masculine plural accusative. With only 9 Quranic occurrences of this root (7 as NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), this is an uncommon root.

NOUN_CONCRETE accusative (manṣūb, object of wajadnā). Root ʾ-b-w. Broken plural of ʾab (father). Suffixed with -nā (our). The noun functions as the first object in a double-accusative construction with wajadnā.

NOUN_CONCRETE functioning as khabar (predicate) of inna, in nominative case (marfūʿ). Morphologically singular (faʿūl pattern) but semantically applied to the plural pronoun -hum. The faʿūl pattern can function as both singular and plural in Arabic, and ʿaduww is a canonical example of this phenomenon (cf. 2:36, 7:24, 20:123).

NOUN_CONCRETE in accusative case (manṣūb) as the mustathnā (excepted noun) after illā. First term of an iḍāfa (construct) with al-ʿālamīna. The accusative case applies whether the exception is connected or disconnected (after affirmative inna-clause with illā, the mustathnā takes naṣb).

NOUN_ABSTRACT in genitive case (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi in the iḍāfa rabb al-ʿālamīn. The -īna suffix is the masculine sound plural oblique ending. The word ʿālamīn is the plural of ʿālam (world/realm), itself from the root ʿ-l-m which also yields ʿilm (knowledge) and ʿalāma (sign/marker).

Gerund (maṣdar), indefinite, genitive (majrūr by fī). Root ḍ-l-l: to go astray, to lose the way, to err. The indefinite form (ḍalālin rather than al-ḍalāl) may suggest: one instance of error among possible many, or an unspecified/unquantified error — the tanwīn on the indefinite gerund leaves the scope open.

Active participle of Form IV (ʾabāna, yubīnu), indefinite, genitive, agreeing with ḍalālin. From b-y-n: to be clear, to separate, to make manifest. B-sh-r's Quranic sense: bashar denotes the human being in its physical, mortal, creaturely aspect — the creature of flesh and blood, as distinct from malak (angel) or jinn. The indefinite tanwīn on basharun is significant: "a human being" (not even "the human being") — the indefinite predicate underscores ordinariness. In Thamūd's challenge, calling Ṣāliḥ bashar is a category-reduction: he is not prophet, not messenger, not divinely exceptional — just one member of the human biological type.

Noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT), nominative (marfūʿ), with first-person plural possessive suffix -nā (genitive). Mithlu is in construct (iḍāfa) with the pronominal suffix -nā. Grammatically, mithlunā functions as a second predicative/adjective modifying basharun: "a human being [who is] like us." ROOT_LEXICON: 169 occurrences; NOUN_ABSTRACT: 163 (dominant). M-th-l's core sense: likeness, similarity, equality of type. In v.154, mithlunā is the social weapon: Ṣāliḥ is not merely human in general (basharun) but specifically equal to Thamūd — their peer, their mithil. The suffix -nā (us) includes all of Thamūd in the comparison, denying Ṣāliḥ any elevation above his community.

Noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT), genitive (majrūr) indefinite, governed by the preposition bi-. ROOT_LEXICON: 382 Quranic occurrences; NOUN_ABSTRACT: 382 (the only form). Ā-y-y's core Quranic sense: āya (sign/token/miracle/verse) — that which points beyond itself to a signified reality. In prophetic narratives, āya in the challenge context means a miraculous sign demonstrating divine backing: not a natural phenomenon but an extraordinary event that only divine power can produce. The indefinite āyatin (a sign) is deliberately open: any sufficiently extraordinary sign will count. In the immediate narrative, God's response is the she-camel of v.155.

Noun (NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), definite (al-), genitive (majrūr) plural, governed by mina. Form I active participle (fāʿilīna pattern): ṣādiq = one who tells the truth, one who is sincere. ROOT_LEXICON: 155 occurrences; NOUN_ACTIVE_PART: 84 (dominant). Ṣ-d-q's core sense: truth, truthfulness, sincerity, correspondence between word and reality. The active participle ṣādiq denotes one who is characteristically truthful — not merely speaking truth on one occasion but being of truthful character. In the challenge context, mina l-ṣādiqīn frames Ṣāliḥ's truthfulness as a testable claim: prophetic credentials require membership in the class of the veracious.

Noun, NOUN_CONCRETE, feminine, indefinite (tanwīn ḍamma), nominative — functioning as the predicate (PRED/khabar) of the nominal sentence hādhihi nāqatun. Root n-w-q: "she-camel, female camel." ROOT_LEXICON: 7 occurrences, TIER: uncommon, all NOUN_CONCRETE — this root appears exclusively as a noun in the Quran, never verbally. Indefinite nāqatun (a she-camel) rather than definite al-nāqa.

Noun, NOUN_CONCRETE, masculine, indefinite (tanwīn ḍamma), nominative — functioning as the delayed subject (mubtadaʾ muʾakhkhar) in the clause lahā shirbun. ROOT_LEXICON: 39 occurrences, TIER: common; NOUN_CONCRETE: 14 occurrences. The noun shirb = the allocated share or portion of water in a communal water-distribution system — a legal-technical term in classical Arabic. The QIRAAT variant shurb (ḍamma on shin) vs. shirb (kasra) carries a possible semantic nuance.

Noun, NOUN_CONCRETE, masculine, nominative, construct state (muḍāf) — governed by yawmin maʿlūmin (genitive). The construct state marks shirbu as the head noun of the iḍāfa chain shirbu yawmin maʿlūmin (the water-right of a known day). This is the second occurrence of the sh-r-b noun in the ayah — first as indefinite shirbun (word 6, for the she-camel), now as construct-state shirbu (for Thamūd). The construct form removes the tanwīn and binds shirbu tightly to yawmin maʿlūmin.

Noun, NOUN_ABSTRACT, masculine, indefinite (tanwīn kasra), genitive (majrūr) — as muḍāf ilayh (genitive complement) of shirbu, and as muḍāf itself governing maʿlūmin in adjectival agreement. ROOT_LEXICON: 249 occurrences, all NOUN_ABSTRACT. In the construct shirbu yawmin maʿlūmin, yawm is the time-unit that bounds Thamūd's water allocation. The indefinite yawmin (a day) with the adjective maʿlūmin (known) = "a day that is known" — a specific day within a communal schedule already understood by all parties.

Noun, NOUN_PASSIVE_PART (Form IV passive participle from aʿlama = to inform/designate), functioning as ADJ modifying yawmin — in agreement (genitive, masculine, indefinite). ROOT_LEXICON: 854 occurrences, TIER: very_common. NOUN_PASSIVE_PART: 11 occurrences of maʿlūm. From ʿ-l-m: "to know, to learn, to mark/designate." The "known day" (yawm maʿlūm) is a day that has been made known, officially designated.

Noun (gerund/masdar from s-w-ʾ), indefinite, genitive (majrūr, governed by bi). ROOT_LEXICON: 171 Quranic occurrences; GERUND:45 (dominant form); NOUN_ABSTRACT:63; TRANSITIVITY: IV MIXED. The indefinite sūʾin (tanwīn, no article) means "any harm" — there is no threshold; any degree of harmful contact is forbidden.

Noun (abstract), nominative (marfūʿ) as subject of yaʾkhudha-kum, in construct state (muḍāf) governing yawmin. ROOT_LEXICON: 373 Quranic occurrences; NOUN_ABSTRACT:231 (overwhelmingly dominant form); GERUND:91; TRANSITIVITY: IV TRANS, PV TRANS. The root ʿ-dh-b denotes punishment, torment, chastisement — the Quran's primary term for divine retributive consequence. In the iḍāfa ʿadhābu yawmin ʿaẓīmin, ʿadhābu is the muḍāf (governed noun), denoting the punishment that "belongs to" or "comes with" the great day. As the grammatical subject of yaʾkhudha-kum, the punishment is personified as the seizing agent — a standard Quranic figure where the ʿadhāb actively "takes hold" of the punished.

Noun (abstract), indefinite, genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayh of ʿadhābu, itself in construct state (muḍāf) governing ʿaẓīmin. ROOT_LEXICON: 249 Quranic occurrences; NOUN_ABSTRACT:249 (exclusively nominal). The root y-w-m is the standard Arabic term for "day." In the Quran, yawm appears in multiple senses: the ordinary day (24 hours), the day of a particular event (the day of the battle, the day of judgment), and the eschatological "Day" (yawm al-qiyāma, yawm al-dīn). In yawmin ʿaẓīmin, yawm is indefinite and qualified as great — "a day great in its proportions," connoting a specific future day of enormous magnitude and consequence.

Adjective (qualitative, mufiʿlīna pattern: ʿaẓīm from ʿ-ẓ-m), indefinite, genitive (majrūr) agreeing with yawmin. ROOT_LEXICON: 128 Quranic occurrences; ADJ_QUALIT:100 (dominant form); top co-occ. with ʾ-l-h (69), ʿ-dh-b (26), k-w-n (25). The adjective ʿaẓīm is the primary Quranic superlative-scale qualifier for things of maximum magnitude — the enormity that exceeds ordinary measure. Applied to yawm (day), it characterizes the day as one of overwhelming scale, catastrophic consequence, and total magnitude — a day so great that its punishment can be defined by the day's greatness alone.

Noun (active participle, fāʿilīna pattern), definite by context (predicate of aṣbaḥū), accusative/predicate (khabar), plural masculine. From n-d-m: "to regret, feel remorse, be sorry." ROOT_LEXICON: 7 Quranic occurrences; NOUN_ACTIVE_PART:5 dominant; GERUND:2. TRANSITIVITY: —. The root n-d-m denotes the psychological state of regret over something done — remorse after an irreversible act. Nādimīna as active participle (not gerund) marks the state as presently and characteristically obtaining: they are in the state of being regretful, not merely that regret happened to them once. As khabar (predicate) of aṣbaḥū, nādimīna completes the stative-change construction: "they became ones-who-are-regretful."

Noun (GERUND functioning as concrete agent-noun), nominative (marfūʿ) as fāʿil (grammatical agent) of ʾakhadha; definite (al-); root ʿ-dh-b = to torment, chastise, punish; the root also carries the ironic opposite sense "to be sweet/easy" (ʿadhb = sweet water)

Noun (ism / NOUN_ABSTRACT from ʾ-y-y), accusative (manṣūb) as ism of inna, indefinite (tanwīn), singular; āya = something that points beyond itself to a reality; root ʾ-y-y appears exclusively as NOUN_ABSTRACT (382 occurrences) with no verbal forms in the Quran

Noun (active participle, NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), Form IV (mufiʿlīna pattern = muʾminīna), masculine plural, accusative (manṣūb) as khabar kāna; root ʾ-m-n = security, trust, faith; Form IV āmana = to enter a state of security through trust

Noun (ism), accusative (manṣūb) as ism inna, with 2ms possessive pronoun -ka (muḍāf ilayhi). The -ka addresses the Prophet (Muḥammad), personalizing the divine relationship at the close of the Ṣāliḥ narrative. The rabb who authorized Ṣāliḥ's mission, provided the she-camel as a sign, and ultimately enacted the punishment on Thamūd is "your lord" — the Prophet's own sustaining authority. ROOT_LEXICON: 975 occurrences; 968 as NOUN_CONCRETE; top co-occ with ʿ-z-z: 22×, with r-ḥ-m: 92×.

Divine name / intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern), definite (al-), nominative (marfūʿ) as first khabar (predicate) of inna. ROOT_LEXICON: 120 occurrences; NOUN_PROP:64 (dominant as divine name); ADJ_QUALIT:37; top co-occ: ʾ-l-h:69, ḥ-k-m:49, ʿ-l-m:22, r-b-b:22, q-w-l:21. The faʿīl pattern marks enduring inherent quality (not occasional: ʿazīz = constitutionally invincible). In the Ṣāliḥ context, al-ʿazīzu is the attribute of God that explains why the punishment of Thamūd was both real and inescapable — the extraordinary material achievement of the mountain-carvers (v.149) could not exempt them from divine consequence.

Divine name / intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern), definite (al-), nominative (marfūʿ) as second khabar (predicate) of inna, parallel to al-ʿazīzu. ROOT_LEXICON: 339 occurrences; NOUN_PROP:91; ADJ_INTENS:61; top co-occ: ʾ-l-h:130, r-b-b:92, gh-f-r:91, k-w-n:64, ʾ-m-n:59. In the Ṣāliḥ context, ar-raḥīmu is the attribute that explains the prophetic mission itself, the she-camel as mercy-sign, and the three-day warning before punishment — each element of the Thamūd narrative was a mercy-extension before the consequence of ʿizzat Allāh arrived. The faʿīl pattern (enduring relational quality) means raḥīm is not an occasional act but a constitutional attribute operating throughout the entire Ṣāliḥ-Thamūd encounter.

Proper noun (NOUN_PROP), nominative (tanwīn ḍamma: -un), serving as appositive (badal or ʿaṭf bayān) to akhūhum — the name follows and specifies the "brother." ROOT_LEXICON: 27 Quranic occurrences; NOUN_PROP:21 (dominant); NOUN_PROP_FOREIGN:6. The name Lūṭ is of Semitic origin (cognate with Hebrew Lot). As a NOUN_PROP, it is indeclinable in Arabic but receives tanwīn in some traditions (lūṭun) because it is used without the article al-. The nominative tanwīn (ḍammatān) on Lūṭun is standard in this ayah. Top co-occurrences from ROOT_LEXICON: q-w-l:13 (said), q-w-m:12 (people), r-s-l:8 (messenger/sent) — confirming Lūṭ's Quranic profile as a prophet who speaks to his people and is identified as a messenger.

Noun, concrete (ism), indefinite nominative (marfūʿ) — khabar of inna. From r-s-l: "to send, to dispatch." The faʿūl pattern (rasūl) is an intensive/passive form = "one who is sent repeatedly" or "one whose sending is emphatic." Indefiniteness here is significant: not al-rasūl (the specific known messenger) but rasūlun (a messenger, one of a type) — the claim is category membership, not unique identity.

Adjective, qualitative (ṣifa), indefinite nominative (marfūʿ) — either modifying rasūlun (adjectival reading) or serving as a second khabar of inna (predicative reading). From ʾ-m-n: "to be safe, to trust, to be faithful." The faʿīl pattern (amīn) carries both active sense ("one who is faithful/trusting") and passive sense ("one who is trusted/secured"). Classical: al-amīn was Muhammad's pre-prophetic epithet. The 14 ADJ_QUALIT occurrences in the Quran include this five-fold refrain and other contexts (e.g., al-rūḥ al-amīn at 26:193 for the Holy Spirit — making amīn a recurring quality-marker within this very surah, and al-bayt al-amīn at 95:3 for Mecca).

Proper noun (NOUN_PROP), accusative (manṣūb) as direct object of ittaqū. ROOT_LEXICON: 2853 Quranic occurrences; 2704 as NOUN_PROP. The name Allāh = definite al- + ilāh (the God, the object of worship). Root ʾ-l-h carries sense of "to be bewildered, to seek refuge" — God is the refuge of the perplexed. In the Lūṭ pericope, the people are not polytheists per se but transgressors — Lūṭ's command to fear specifically Allāh names the ultimate moral authority against whom their behavior is measured.

Indefinite noun (ism nakira), genitive case (majrūr by min). GERUND form of ʾ-j-r, with 92 GERUND occurrences in the Quran. Here it denotes the payment that Lūṭ disclaims — any material or social compensation for delivering the message to his people.

Noun (GERUND), genitive construct with 1st person singular possessive pronoun -ya (-ī). Same root as word 6 (ajrin), now with possessive attachment — "my ajr." This is the ajr that Lūṭ claims from God, contrasting with the ajr he disclaims from his people.

Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), genitive (majrūr by ʿalā), first term of iḍāfa (genitive construct) with al-ʿālamīna. R-b-b has 968 NOUN_CONCRETE occurrences — the most frequent nominal form in the Quran. Here used without the definite article, in construct state with ʿālamīna.

Noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT per MASAQ), genitive plural (majrūr as second term of iḍāfa with rabb). Sound masculine plural form. From ʿ-l-m: root meaning "to know" — ʿālam (world) is etymologically "that by which one knows" or "a realm of being." 854 total root occurrences; NOUN_ABSTRACT: 78.

NOUN_CONCRETE, definite (al-), accusative (OBJ of tatūna), masculine plural. Root dh-k-r: COUNT 292, TIER very_common; NOUN_CONCRETE:20 (of 292 total occurrences). The word dhukar/dhukrān is the plural of dhakar (male), a concrete noun used here for male human beings. The dominant senses of dh-k-r are remembrance/reminder (GERUND:88, IV:66, CV:55) and males (NOUN_CONCRETE:20).

NOUN_ABSTRACT, definite (al-), genitive (muḍāf ilayhi governed by min), masculine sound plural (-īna). Root ʿ-l-m: COUNT 854, TIER very_common; NOUN_ABSTRACT:78 occurrences including al-ʿālamīn; TOP CO-OCC with ʾ-l-h:409, q-w-l:170, k-w-n:159, r-b-b:130. Al-ʿālamīn in genitive here as the source-category for the PP; immediately following the same phrase rabb al-ʿālamīn in v.164 (the no-wages formula).

Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), nominative (fāʿil of khalaqa), with 2nd person masculine plural possessive suffix -kum. ROOT_LEXICON: 975 occurrences; very_common; NOUN_CONCRETE:968 (dominant form). In Quranic prophetic addresses, rabbukum (your Lord) is the standard possessive divine address — emphasizing the specific relationship between the Lord and the addressed community. Here rabbukum is the grammatical subject (fāʿil) of khalaqa: "YOUR Lord created" — placing the divine-human relationship at the center of the creation act. The abandonment of God's provision is thus an abandonment of what the people's own sustainer/lord fashioned for them.

Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), plural (azwāj) of zawj (mate, pair, spouse), genitive (governed by min), with 2nd person masculine plural possessive suffix -kum. ROOT_LEXICON: 81 occurrences; NOUN_CONCRETE:76 (dominant); TRANSITIVITY: IV TRANS, PV TRANS. The root z-w-j means "pair, mate, couple" — zawj is both "a member of a pair" and "one's pair/mate/spouse." In the Quran, azwāj is used for spouses/mates and also for the cosmic pairing-principle (51:49: wa-min kulli shayʾin khalaqnā zawjayn = "from everything We created a pair"). The possessive -kum makes these the people's own mates — not abstract creation but their specific, personally-provided mates.

Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), indefinite (no definite article, but with tanwīn -un), nominative, functioning as khabar (predicate) of the nominal sentence with antum as mubtadaʾ. ROOT_LEXICON: 660 occurrences; very_common; NOUN_CONCRETE:383 (dominant); top co-occ with ʾ-l-h (242), q-w-l (153), k-w-n (131). Qawm in the Quran is the standard term for a social community as a coherent collective — the addressable unit of prophetic mission. The indefinite form qawmun (a people) here is predicative: "you are [a] people characterized by ʿ-w-d transgression." The qawm frame collectivizes the verdict: this is not the judgment of individuals but the characterization of a social group as a whole.

Noun (NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), Form I active participle masculine plural (fāʿilūna → ʿādūna), indefinite. ROOT_LEXICON: 68 occurrences; common; FORMS: IV:24, NOUN_ACTIVE_PART:8 (confirmed form here), PV:8; top co-occ: ʾ-l-h (24), k-w-n (14), q-w-m (13). From root ʿ-w-d meaning "to return, to go back, to repeat; to transgress, to exceed limits." The NOUN_ACTIVE_PART (ʿādūna, pl. of ʿādin) means "transgressors, those who habitually exceed limits." The root ʿ-w-d carries a dual semantic: (1) to return/repeat (ʿāda ilā = he returned to); and (2) to transgress/exceed (ʿadā ʿalā = he transgressed against). The active participle ʿādūna here is the verdict: these people are, by habitual and defining nature, transgressors/boundary-crossers. The form ʿādūna is distinct from ʿĀdūna (the people ʿĀd) — here without the proper-noun connotation.

Noun (GERUND of Form I ʿamila, used as a concrete noun), genitive (majrūr by the lām preposition), with second person masculine plural suffix -kum (your). From ʿ-m-l: "to do, work, act, practice." ROOT_LEXICON: 360 occurrences, 32 GERUND, TIER: very_common. ʿAmal encompasses the full range of human activity: deed, action, practice, work, conduct. Here with -kum (plural you), it refers to the ʿamal of Lot's people collectively — in context, the ʿamal specifically identified in vv.165-166: the sexual approach of men (ataʾtūna al-dhukrāna, v.165) and the leaving of wives. The singular ʿamal (not plural aʿmāl) treats the transgression as a unified practice, a single definable act, rather than a collection of miscellaneous wrongs.

Noun (NOUN_ACTIVE_PART), definite with article al-, genitive plural (majrūr by min). From q-w-l in the sense of qalā (not qāla): the root q-w-l has two distinct semantic registers: (1) qāla = to say/speak and (2) qalā = to detest, abhor, be averse to. Al-qālīna is the Form I active participle plural of qalā: qālin (sg.) → qālīna (plural genitive). ROOT_LEXICON: 1337 occurrences dominated by the "to say" register. Lane's distinguishes qalā (present yaqlu, II yaqllī?) from qāla (present yaqūlu). Classical tafsīr (Ṭabarī: al-qālūna lahu = those who abhor it intensely, from qalā = al-bughḍ al-shadīd; Zamakhsharī: qalā = karaha karāhatan shadīdatan = hated with intense hatred). This is one of the rare Quranic instances where q-w-l's "abhorrence" register is deployed — making it the rarer, more marked reading of the root.

Noun (rabb), vocative case, first person singular possessive suffix -ī (contracted in pause/construct: rabbi). No ḥarf nidāʾ (no yā): the bare vocative rabbi is the standard Quranic form for urgent, intimate du'ā address. ROOT_LEXICON: 975 Quranic occurrences; NOUN_CONCRETE:968 (dominant); tier very_common; confidence verified. Top co-occurrences: q-w-l (260), ʾ-l-h (204), k-w-n (164), ʿ-l-m (130). Rabb encompasses: lord, master, sustainer, nurturer, owner, the one who rears/tends — the relational term par excellence for the divine-human address in personal prayer. In du'ā, rabbi functions as the supreme warrant for the petition: "you who are my sustainer, save me." The QIRAAT note records a variant rabbu (nominative, CE variant) — the standard is rabbi (genitive/vocative with ī).

Noun (ahl), genitive (in construct with ī suffix — possessive iḍāfa: ahlī = "my ahl/family"), functioning as second object coordinated by wa to the -nī suffix of najjinī. ROOT_LEXICON: 132 Quranic occurrences; NOUN_CONCRETE:128 (dominant); NOUN_ABSTRACT:4; tier very_common; confidence qac_preferred. Top co-occurrences: ʾ-l-h (47), q-w-l (39), k-w-n (35), k-t-b (33), ʾ-m-n (28). Ahl's semantic range: (1) family, household (those who belong to a dwelling); (2) people of a place (ahl al-madīna = people of the city); (3) worthy of / fit for something (ahlun li-kadha = suited to something). In the Lot narrative context, ahlī = the members of Lot's household — specifically his family who believe, anticipating the exception of the wife noted in v.171 (illa ʿajūzan fī l-ghābirīn).

Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), accusative (manṣūb) as second coordinated object of najjaynā, in construct state with attached 3ms pronoun -hu (his). ROOT_LEXICON: 132 occurrences; NOUN_CONCRETE:128 (dominant form); TIER: very_common; CONFIDENCE: qac_preferred; TOP CO-OCC: أ ل ه:47, ق و ل:39. Root ʾ-h-l: ahl = family, household, people belonging to one, those fit for something. The word encompasses nuclear family, extended household, members of a community or group. In prophetic rescue narratives, ahl refers to those within the prophet's household-sphere who share in his deliverance.

Noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT in MASAQ tagging — functions as tawkīd maʿnawī, semantic emphasis/corroboration), accusative masculine plural (-īna). From Form IV afʿal pattern: ajmaʿ. ROOT_LEXICON: 129 occurrences; NOUN_ABSTRACT:79 (dominant form); TIER: very_common; TOP CO-OCC: أ ل ه:53, ك و ن:25, ق و ل:25. The word functions grammatically as tawkīd (corroborative emphasis) for the combined object (najjaynāhu wa-ahlahū) — not a predicate or modifier but an emphatic intensifier insisting on completeness. Classical grammarians restrict ajmaʿ/ajmaʿīna to the tawkīd function.

Adjective used nominally (ADJ_QUALIT functioning as a noun), accusative singular indefinite, functioning as the mustathnā (excepted element) after illā. Root ʿ-j-z: to be weak, to fail, to be incapacitated; ʿajūz (Form faʿūl) = one who has become old/weak. ROOT_LEXICON: 26 Quranic occurrences; ADJ_QUALIT:4 (always referring to the old woman in Lot-narrative contexts or elderly persons). The faʿūl form often indicates a dispositional or state-based quality: ʿajūz = one who is in a state of being incapacitated/old. Indefinite form (ʿajūzan without al-) presents her as a type-figure rather than a named individual — she is categorized by condition, not identified by name.

Noun (active participle, fāʿilīna pattern from Form I ghabara), definite (al-), genitive (majrūr) plural as object of preposition fī. ROOT_LEXICON: 8 Quranic occurrences; NOUN_ACTIVE_PART:7; NOUN_CONCRETE:1. Root gh-b-r: to remain behind, to linger when others depart, to be left over/remaining. The active participle al-ghābirīna = those who are (presently) in the state of remaining behind. Appears exclusively in the Lūṭ narrative across its 7 active-participle occurrences: 7:83, 11:81, 15:60, 26:171, 27:57, 29:32, 29:33, 37:135. Root meanings: (1) shaʿaba = to divide, split, branch; (2) shuʿba = branch, tributary, division; (3) shaʿb = a people/nation (plural: shuʿūb — cf. 49:13 jaʿalnākum shuʿūban); (4) shaʿb = a pass between two mountains; (5) al-ayka (thicket/forest) relates to dense branching vegetation — creating a resonance between the prophet's name and his community's defining habitat. CRITICAL structural note: Shuʿaybun here functions as the lone subject (fāʿil) without the preceding akhūhum that all four previous prophets carry in the formula. In Shuʿayb's other Quranic appearances (7:85, 11:84, 29:36 — the Madyan mission), he IS called akhūhum. The absence here marks the aṣḥāb al-ayka as a different, non-brother community.

Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), accusative indefinite (manṣūb, tanwīn). Direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of ānastu. Root n-w-r. 146 occurrences as NOUN_CONCRETE in the Quran. The indefinite form nāran (a fire, not the fire) indicates Moses encounters an unidentified fire — its nature is unknown to him.

Noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT), genitive indefinite (majrūr by bi-, tanwīn). Root kh-b-r. 52 occurrences in the Quran, predominantly as the divine attribute al-Khabīr (the All-Aware, 43x as ADJ_QUALIT). Here used as NOUN_ABSTRACT (5 total) meaning "news, information, report."

Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), genitive indefinite (majrūr by bi-, tanwīn). Root sh-h-b. Rare root with only 5 total Quranic occurrences, all as NOUN_CONCRETE. The word shihāb carries a fundamental dual meaning: a torch/firebrand (terrestrial) and a shooting star/meteor (celestial).

Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), genitive indefinite (majrūr, tanwīn). In the standard reading, qabasin is in apposition (badal or ʿaṭf bayān) to shihābin — "a brand, [that is] a burning one." Root q-b-s. Rare root with only 3 Quranic occurrences. In the variant reading (iḍāfa), qabasin is the muḍāf ilayhi of shihāb.

Concrete noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), nominative case (apposition to the vocative ayyuhā). Definite with al-. 329 Quranic occurrences as NOUN_CONCRETE — among the most frequent nouns. The root ʾ-n-s relates to human sociability and perception.

Abstract noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT), accusative case (object of ʿullimnā). Maṣdar/noun of place-and-manner from Form I naṭaqa. Only 1 occurrence as NOUN_ABSTRACT in Quran — this is it. The root n-ṭ-q has 12 total Quranic occurrences (IV:9, PV:2). The manṭiq form (noun of instrument/manner) implies structured, articulate speech — not mere sound.

Concrete noun (NOUN_CONCRETE), genitive case (second term of iḍāfa: manṭiq al-ṭayr). Definite with al-. 20 occurrences as NOUN_CONCRETE. The root ṭ-y-r fundamentally means "to fly" — ṭayr is a collective noun for flying creatures.

Abstract noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT), genitive case (second term of iḍāfa with kull), indefinite (tanwīn). 283 Quranic occurrences. The most general ontological term in Arabic — any entity, concept, or event that can be referenced.

Gerund/verbal noun (GERUND), nominative case (predicate of inna via la-huwa). Definite with al-. 86 occurrences as GERUND in Quran. The root f-ḍ-l relates to excess, surplus, superiority, and gracious giving.

Noun, indefinite, genitive (majrūr by مِنْ). Root sh-y-ʾ: "to will, to wish" (classical); derivative: "a thing that exists" = that which has been willed into being. 283 Quranic occurrences — the most general noun in Arabic. Indefinite + tanwīn under negation/condition = universal quantifier.

Noun, nominative, definite by iḍāfa (construct state with الْحَيَاةِ). Root m-t-ʿ: "to enjoy, to use, to furnish with provisions." مَتَاع = that which is enjoyed temporarily; classical: goods for a journey, provisions that are consumed. Predicate of the relative/conditional clause. Nominative as khabar.

Verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund), definite with al-, genitive by iḍāfa (مَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ). Root ḥ-y-y: "to live, to be alive." الْحَيَاة = life, living, existence. 83 occurrences as gerund. In construct with الدُّنْيَا — "the life of the near world."

Noun/adjective, definite, genitive (adjective following الْحَيَاةِ in iḍāfa chain). Root d-n-w: "to be near, to approach, to be low." الدُّنْيَا is the feminine elative (comparative/superlative): "the nearer/nearest" or "the lower/lowest." 115 occurrences as noun. Functions as both a spatial descriptor (nearest realm) and a value judgment (lowest realm).

Noun, nominative (coordinated with مَتَاعُ), definite by pronoun suffix -hā (referring to الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا). Root z-y-n: "to adorn, to beautify, to make attractive." زِينَة = adornment, ornament, beauty. 13 occurrences as noun abstract. The pronoun suffix links adornment specifically to the worldly life — it is not free-standing beauty but attached decoration.

Proper noun, genitive (governed by عِنْدَ). Root '-l-h: "to worship, to be bewildered, to seek refuge." اللَّه = the proper name of God in Arabic. 2704 occurrences as NOUN_PROP. Here functions as the possessor/custodian of the superior goods.

Comparative adjective (ism tafḍīl), nominative, indefinite. Root kh-y-r: "to choose, to prefer, to be good." خَيْرٌ as elative = "better/best" (comparative/superlative). 101 occurrences as ADJ_COMP. Functions as the first of two predicates for مَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ — what is with God is "better."

Comparative adjective (ism tafḍīl), nominative, indefinite. Root b-q-y: "to remain, to last, to endure, to survive." أَبْقَى = "more lasting/enduring" (elative). 7 occurrences as ADJ_COMP. Second predicate of مَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ. Paired with خَيْرٌ to assert both qualitative superiority and temporal durability.

Accusative definite noun, object of ibtagh. Al-dār = the abode/dwelling. Root d-w-r = to revolve, cycle, turn. The "abode" is etymologically a place one returns to cyclically, not a static destination.

Accusative definite active participle (feminine), adjectival modifier of al-dār. From '-kh-r = to delay, come after, be last. The ākhira is structurally "that which comes after" — a temporal-sequential marker, not a fixed eschatological term.
Accusative indefinite noun + 2nd person possessive pronoun -ka. Object of tansa. From n-ṣ-b = to erect, set up, plant. Naṣīb = that which is set up/established for someone — an allotted share.
Genitive definite noun (governed by min). From d-n-w = to be near, low, close. Al-dunyā = the nearest, the lowest — the proximate world as opposed to the ākhira.
Proper noun, nominative (subject of aḥsana). God as the agent of excellence — the second of three divine-name occurrences in the ayah.
Accusative definite verbal noun (maṣdar), object of tabghi. From f-s-d = to be spoiled, corrupted, ruined. Al-fasād = the abstract concept of corruption/ruin.
Genitive definite noun (governed by fī). Al-arḍ = the earth, land, ground. The definite article marks the totality of the terrestrial domain.
Accusative proper noun (ism of inna). Third occurrence of the divine name in this ayah, now as the subject of the theological axiom about not loving corrupters.

Accusative definite masculine plural active participle of Form IV (mufsid). Object of yuḥibbu. Those who actively cause corruption — the agents of fasād (word 24). The definite article + active participle = a permanent category of actors, not occasional offenders.

NOUN_ABSTRACT — genitive (governed by fī), with 3ms possessive pronoun -hī. From root z-y-n: to beautify, adorn, embellish. Zīna = the resulting state or means of adornment.

NOUN_ABSTRACT — accusative (subject of layta). Mithla = likeness, equivalent, model. They do not wish for Qārūn's exact possessions but for their EQUIVALENT — mithla preserves a distinction between copy and original.

NOUN_PROP_FOREIGN — nominative (passive subject of ūtiya). A non-Arabic proper noun, identified with biblical Korah (Numbers 16). The name may echo q-r-n (horn/era/companion) to Arabic ears, though it is classified as foreign and indeclinable for triptotic pattern but here takes ḍamma as proxy nominative.

NOUN_ABSTRACT — genitive (governed by dhū in genitive construct). From root ḥ-ẓ-ẓ: portion, lot, share of fortune. A rare root in the Quran (COUNT: 7), always as NOUN_ABSTRACT. The doubled final radical (geminate) gives phonetic weight.
ADJ_QUALIT — genitive (adjective modifying ḥaẓẓin), indefinite with tanwīn. From root ʿ-ẓ-m: greatness, magnitude, bone. A very common Quranic qualifier (100 occurrences as adjective).
Verbal noun/gerund (GERUND), accusative (OBJ), definite with al-. Object of ūtū. The definite article marks this as a specific, known body of knowledge — not any knowledge but THE knowledge.

Abstract noun (NOUN_ABSTRACT) + 2nd person plural pronoun suffix -kum. Cognate accusative function (COGN). An exclamatory expression of lament/warning. All 40 Quranic occurrences are NOUN_ABSTRACT — no verbal forms attested in Quran.
Verbal noun/gerund (GERUND), nominative (SUBJ), in an iḍāfa construct with Allāh. Subject of the nominal sentence thawābu llāhi khayrun. 13 GERUND occurrences in Quran.
Proper noun (NOUN_PROP), genitive (GEN_CONS) — second member of the iḍāfa thawābu llāhi. The genitive marks God as the source/owner of the reward.
Comparative adjective (ADJ_COMP), nominative (PRED), indefinite. Predicate of the nominal sentence thawābu llāhi khayrun. 101 ADJ_COMP occurrences make this the dominant form of kh-y-r in Quran.

Definite qualitative adjective (ADJ_QUALIT) in genitive case, functioning as naʿt (attributive adjective) for ٱلْقُرْءَانِ. Pattern faʿīl = intensive/continuous: one that possesses ḥikma permanently. From ḥ-k-m: to judge, to be wise, to restrain, to perfect.

Indefinite noun, genitive case (majrūr) governed by ʿalā. Abstract noun denoting a defined traversable course. The indefinite tanwīn (-in) contrasts with the definite aṣ-ṣirāṭa in 1:6 — this is "a path" not "THE path." The tanwīn carries mīm-ikhfāʾ (ṣirāṭim-mustaqīmin) before the mīm of mustaqīm.

Active participle of Form X (istaqāma), indefinite genitive (majrūr), functioning as adjective (naʿt) for ṣirāṭin. Form X istafʿala adds reflexive-estimative meaning to root q-w-m (to stand): "that which seeks to establish itself upright." Active participle indicates an ongoing dynamic state, not a completed or static condition.

Form II verbal noun (gerund/maṣdar) in accusative case (manṣūb). Functions as mafʿūl muṭlaq (cognate accusative) reinforcing the verbal meaning implied from 36:2. Pattern tafʿīl indicates intensive/repetitive action — gradual, stage-by-stage descent. First term of an iḍāfa (genitive construct) with al-ʿAzīz.

Definite proper noun in genitive (majrūr), functioning as the second term of the iḍāfa with tanzīla — "sending-down OF the Mighty." Pattern faʿīl indicates a permanent, inherent quality. Also functions as first element in a paired divine-name construction with al-Raḥīm.

Definite proper noun in genitive (majrūr), functioning as naʿt (adjective) for al-ʿAzīz or as a second iḍāfa term in apposition. Pattern faʿīl indicates a continuous, inherent quality — one who is constantly and actively merciful. Completes the divine-name pair ʿAzīz + Raḥīm.

Elative/comparative noun-adjective in genitive after عَلَىٰ; in iḍāfa with suffix pronoun هُمْ, quantifying a referenced group.

Broken plural noun (singular: ʿunuq), genitive (majrūr) governed by fī. Attached possessive pronoun -him (their). The plural aʿnāq can refer to necks literally or to leaders/chiefs (metaphorical extension: the "neck" of a group).

Broken plural noun (singular: ghull), accusative indefinite (mafʿūl bihi — direct object of jaʿalnā). Pattern afʿāl indicates plural of instruments or implements. The tanwīn marks indefiniteness — unspecified collars, their nature left open.

Definite broken plural noun (singular: dhaqan), genitive (majrūr) governed by ilā. The root dh-q-n is rare in the Quran (3 occurrences only). All three occurrences involve movement toward or against the chin — prostration or forced upward orientation.

Passive participle (ism mafʿūl), Form IV (ʾifʿāl → muqmaḥ), masculine plural nominative. Functions as predicate (khabar) of the preceding hum. The root q-m-h is a Quranic hapax — this is its only occurrence in the entire Quran. Pattern muFʿaL indicates the subject is passively affected — they have been forced into this raised-head position.

Noun of place/time in genitive (governed by min). Part of the idiomatic phrase bayna aydī ("before, in the presence of," literally "between the hands of"). Root b-y-n has 295 Quranic occurrences across multiple forms.

Noun, plural (aydī), genitive construct with third person masculine plural pronoun suffix (-him). Broken plural of yad (hand). Here part of the idiom bayna aydī = "before, in the presence of, in front of." Root y-d-y occurs 107 times in the Quran.
Noun, indefinite accusative (manṣūb) functioning as second object of jaʿalnā (mafʿūl bih). Root s-d-d has only 6 Quranic occurrences. Tanwīn (-an) marks indefiniteness — an unspecified barrier.

Noun of place in genitive (governed by min), with third person masculine plural pronoun suffix (-him). Root kh-l-f has 117 Quranic occurrences. Here used as spatial adverb meaning "behind, at the back of."

Noun, indefinite accusative (manṣūb) functioning as second object of the implied jaʿalnā from the first clause. Identical form and function to word 6 — deliberate repetition creating symmetric enclosure.

Abstract noun (maṣdar/noun_abstract) in nominative (marfūʿ), functioning as predicate (khabar) of a suppressed mubtadaʾ or as fronted predicate with the ʾa...ʾam clause as its subject. Pattern faʿāl indicates a state of being level or even. The tanwīn indicates indefiniteness — "a state of equality."
Definite verbal noun/gerund in accusative as object of ittabaʿa; al- makes the reminder a known discourse object.
Definite divine name/title in accusative as object of khashiya. Pattern faʿlān carries intensive or overflowing quality; the title is definite and referential.

Qualitative adjective in genitive agreeing with ajrin; marks the reward as noble/generous in quality, rank, and source.
Qualitative adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), plural, definite with al-, functioning as the object (mafʿūl bihi) of nuḥyī. Pattern fawʿalā (mawtā) is the plural of mayyit (dead person).

Noun (abstract/concrete), plural of athar, with attached 3rd person masculine plural pronoun -hum. In the accusative (manṣūb) as second object coordinated with mā qaddamū. Root '-th-r means trace, imprint, effect, consequence.

Abstract noun functioning as a universal quantifier, in the accusative (manṣūb) as a fronted object (mafʿūl bihi muqaddam) of aḥṣaynāhu. The fronting creates emphasis: "every thing" is placed before the verb for rhetorical weight. Construct state (muḍāf) with shayʾin.

Abstract noun, indefinite, in the genitive (majrūr) as the second term of the construct state (muḍāf ilayhi) with kulla. Root sh-y-ʾ means to will, to want; shayʾ = a thing, an entity, anything that exists or can be conceived.

Concrete noun, indefinite, in the genitive (majrūr) governed by fī. Root '-m-m means to lead, to head, to be a mother/source. imām = leader, guide, prototype, exemplar, register. The indefiniteness here is significant: "a register" (not "the register") — suggesting the register is one of potentially many, or that its nature is being introduced.

Active participle (ism fāʿil) from Form IV (ʾabāna), indefinite, genitive, functioning as an adjective (ṣifa) modifying imāmin. Form IV ʾabāna = to make clear, to manifest, to reveal. The active participle means "making clear" (active) or "clear" (descriptive).
Indefinite accusative noun functioning as direct object of ḍrib; tanwīn marks an unspecified representative case. Initial shaddah reflects assimilation from preceding -hum in recitation.

Cardinal numeral, masculine dual form in the accusative/genitive case (ithnayn is the oblique form of ithnān). Functions as the direct object (maf'ūl bihi) of arsalnā. The dual number is significant: two messengers, not one, were sent initially.

Passive participle (ism maf'ūl) from Form IV (arsala), masculine plural nominative. Functions as khabar (predicate) of inna, completing the clause: "indeed we [are] sent ones." The passive form emphasizes that they were SENT by someone (God) rather than coming of their own accord.
Indefinite noun, nominative (marfūʿ), functioning as predicate (khabar) in the qaṣr structure. The indefiniteness emphasizes generality: any/every human, not a specific one.

Noun, nominative (marfūʿ), functioning as adjective (ṣifa) modifying bashar, with attached 1st person plural possessive pronoun -nā. Establishes equivalence: the messengers are the SAME kind as the deniers.
Definite proper noun, nominative (marfūʿ), functioning as subject (fāʿil) of anzala. The faʿlān pattern (intensive) indicates one saturated with mercy. Used here as the agent of sending-down.

Indefinite noun, genitive (majrūr), governed by min. In the negative context mā anzala...min shayʾin, it means "not any thing at all." The indefiniteness combined with min after negation creates maximally universal scope.

Verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund) of raḥima, Form I, in the accusative indefinite (tanwīn). Functions as mafʿūl li-ajlih (accusative of cause/purpose): "except [as/for] a mercy." The tanwīn marks indefiniteness — the mercy is unquantified, unbounded in quality. The root r-ḥ-m connects to raḥim (womb), the most primal site of protection and nourishment.

Verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund) of mattaʿa (Form II) or mataʿa (Form I), accusative indefinite (tanwīn). Coordinated with raḥmatan as the second object of the exception clause. Root m-t-ʿ encompasses both enjoyment and utility — the thing used/enjoyed and the act of using/enjoying. The accusative case parallels raḥmatan: both are purposes or causes of the exception.

Abstract noun, genitive indefinite (majrūr bi-ilā, with tanwīn). The genitive case is governed by the preposition ilā. The indefiniteness (tanwīn) is critical: ḥīn is not defined — it could be any stretch of time (death, the Hour, a cosmic epoch). The word itself means a portion of time, a season, a moment — its range from an instant to an era makes it maximally flexible.
Plural noun in genitive construct after bayna, with attached 2nd masculine plural suffix -kum; hand as limb, power, and agency.

Noun (ism), feminine singular, indefinite, genitive case (governed by min). From root '-y-y. Tanwīn with kasra (-in) marks indefiniteness and genitive. The singularity is universalized by the expletive min: "any sign whatsoever." Refers to any form of evidence, marker, or indication from the divine.

Noun (ism), feminine plural, definite (by iḍāfa/construct), genitive case (governed by min). From root '-y-y. The plural form contrasts with the singular āyatin in word 5, establishing the whole-to-part relationship. The construct state (iḍāfa) links it to rabbihim: "the signs of their Lord." Same root as word 5 but in a different grammatical function (PREP_OBJ vs AGNT).

Noun (ism), masculine singular, definite (by iḍāfa + pronoun), genitive case (second term of iḍāfa with āyāti). Root r-b-b. The attached pronoun -him (3rd person masculine plural) refers to the people who turn away. Rabb is in construct with āyāt, making "signs of their Lord" a genitive chain. The choice of rabb (rather than Allāh or ilāh) emphasizes the nurturing, sustaining relationship.

Active participle (ism fāʿil), Form IV (afʿala → muʿriḍ), masculine plural, accusative case (predicate of kāna). Root '-r-d. The active participle describes a settled characteristic, not a momentary action — they are characterized by the quality of turning away. The accusative case is governed by kāna (predicate of the copula). Form IV iʿrāḍ means "to turn away, avert, present one's side/flank." The base root ʿ-r-ḍ means "width, breadth, side, flank" — to turn away is literally to present one's broad side.

Definite noun (gerund/maṣdar), nominative case (marfūʿ) with ḍamma. Functions as apposition (badal) to hādhā or as ʿaṭf bayān (explanatory adjunct). The definite article al- marks the promise as known — previously mentioned or established in discourse. Root و ع د (w-ʿ-d) encompasses both promise (of good) and threat (of evil). MASAQ tags: GERUND, role APPOS.

Active participle (ism fāʿil), masculine plural, genitive/accusative (oblique case) — genitive because it functions as predicate of kāna (V_COP_PRED in MASAQ), agreeing with the subject kuntum. Root ṣ-d-q: to be true, to speak truth, to verify, to fulfill. The active participle denotes a stable quality: not "those who spoke truth once" but "those who ARE truthful" as a defining characteristic. MASAQ tags: NOUN_ACTIVE_PART, role V_COP_PRED.

Noun of instance (maṣdar marrī / gerund of instance), indefinite accusative singular feminine. From root ṣ-y-ḥ. The tāʾ marbūṭa + tanwīn marks it as a single occurrence of the action of shouting — one shout, one cry. Accusative because it is the object of yanẓurūna (the thing awaited). The indefinite form heightens the indeterminacy: "a shout" — unidentified, unspecified, terrifying in its vagueness.

Adjective (ṣifa), indefinite accusative singular feminine. From root w-ḥ-d. Agrees with ṣayḥatan in gender (feminine), number (singular), case (accusative), and definiteness (indefinite). Functions as the qualifier that makes the shout emphatic: not multiple shouts but ONE. The feminine form wāḥida agrees with the grammatically feminine ṣayḥa.

Verbal noun (maṣdar / gerund) of Form II waṣṣā, in the accusative (manṣūb) as the direct object of yastaṭīʿūna. Indefinite (tankīr) with tanwīn — "any bequest at all," the indefiniteness intensifies the negation: not even a single directive. This is the ONLY occurrence of the GERUND form tawṣiya in the entire Quran.

Noun in genitive (majrūr) governed by ilā. Possessive pronoun -him (their, 3rd masculine plural) attached. Functions as the goal of the denied return. Root '-h-l denotes intimate belonging: family, household, those who share a dwelling or bond.
noun, concrete (NOUN_CONCRETE), genitive case (governed by fī), definite (al-)
noun, concrete (NOUN_CONCRETE), genitive case (governed by min), definite (al-), plural
noun, concrete (NOUN_CONCRETE), genitive case (governed by ilā), definite (possessive pronoun -him), construct state
Abstract noun in accusative (manṣūb) as object of the implicit verb of calling (nudba); possessive suffix -nā (our) makes the woe self-directed
Noun of time/place (maf'al pattern) from r-q-d, genitive case governed by min, with 1st person plural possessive suffix -nā
Proper noun (intensive adjective fa'lān pattern) functioning as agent (fā'il) of wa'ada; nominative case; the definite article al- marks it as a unique divine name
Passive participle (ism maf'ūl) from Form IV arsala, masculine plural nominative with definite article; functions as subject (fā'il) of ṣadaqa

Noun of instance (maṣdar marrī / gerund of instance), indefinite accusative singular feminine. From root ṣ-y-ḥ. The tāʾ marbūṭa + tanwīn marks a single occurrence of the action of shouting. Accusative because it is the predicate of kānat (khabar kāna). The indefinite form heightens indeterminacy: "a shout" — unnamed, unspecified. In the canonical-10 variant (ṣayḥatun, nominative), it becomes the subject of kānat. This word appears in nearly identical construction in 36:29 (leading to khāmidūn, extinction) and 36:49 (preceding taʾkhudhuhum, seizure).

Adjective (ṣifa), indefinite accusative singular feminine. From root w-ḥ-d. Agrees with ṣayḥatan in gender (feminine), number (singular), case (accusative), and definiteness (indefinite). Qualifies the shout as singular — not multiple shouts but exactly ONE. The feminine form wāḥida agrees with grammatically feminine ṣayḥa. In the canonical-10 variant (wāḥidatun, nominative), it follows ṣayḥatun as an adjective in the nominative.

Abstract noun functioning as predicate (khabar) or circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl). Nominative indefinite with tanwīn. From root j-m-ʿ. Functions as the first predicate of hum: "they are all / they are altogether." Emphasizes totality — no one is excluded from the assembly. The word operates on two levels: (1) quantitative — every single being, and (2) qualitative — gathered together, assembled as a collective. The NOUN_ABSTRACT form group has HIGH syntactic diversity (6 roles in 79 occurrences), with jamīʿ appearing in CIRCUM (49 times), INTENCIF (24), and PRED (3) among other roles.

Passive participle (ism mafʿūl), Form IV, masculine plural nominative. From root ḥ-ḍ-r. The Form IV (aḥḍara) means "to make present, to bring, to cause to attend." The passive participle muḥḍar means "one who is made present, brought forth, compelled to attend." The plural nominative muḥḍarūna functions as the second predicate of hum (after jamīʿun). The passive voice is critical: they do not attend willingly — they are MADE to attend, BROUGHT by force. The NOUN_PASSIVE_PART form group has 11 occurrences with MEDIUM syntactic diversity (4 roles): CIRCUM (1), PART_COP_PRED (2), PRED (6), PREP_OBJ (2).
NOUN_ABSTRACT — indefinite nominative (marfūʿ) as passive subject (nā'ib al-fāʿil) of tuẓlamu
NOUN_ABSTRACT — indefinite accusative (manṣūb) as cognate accusative or specification of degree

Active participle (ism fāʿil) from Form I ṣaḥiba, functioning as a noun. Accusative case (manṣūb) as ism inna. Plural of ṣāḥib. In construct (iḍāfa) with al-janna, forming the compound "companions of the garden." The active participle form implies ongoing, habitual accompaniment — not a one-time visit but a state of being.

Definite noun (maʿrifa) in the genitive case (majrūr) as the second term of the iḍāfa construction with aṣḥāb. From root j-n-n meaning "to conceal, to cover, to shield." al-janna literally = "the concealed/covered place" — a garden is so called because its trees conceal what is within.

Verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund) of Form I shaghala, in the genitive case (majrūr) as the object of the preposition fī. Indefinite (nakirah) with tanwīn — the indefiniteness creates semantic openness: "an occupation" rather than "the occupation," leaving the nature of the shughl deliberately unspecified. This is the ONLY occurrence of the gerund form shughl in the entire Quran.

Active participle (ism fāʿil) from Form I fakiha, masculine plural nominative (marfūʿ). Functions either as: (a) second predicate (khabar thānī) of inna — an independent assertion that they are delighting; or (b) ḥāl (circumstantial clause) describing their state while in shughl. The wāw-nūn plural ending indicates masculine rational beings. From root f-k-h which carries both "fruit" (fākiha) and "amusement/delight" (fukāha).

Noun, masculine plural (jawmuʿ taksīr of zawj), nominative (marfūʿ) as maʿṭūf on هُمْ. Possessive pronoun -hum attached. Root z-w-j: to pair, to couple. The word azwāj encompasses: (a) marital spouses, (b) kinds/sorts/types, (c) paired counterparts of any nature. In 36:36, the same surah uses al-azwāj for "all pairs" — created kinds. MASAQ tags NOUN_CONCRETE, role CONJ_N.

Noun (ism), indefinite genitive (majrūr by fī). Plural of ẓill (shade, shadow, canopy). Root ẓ-l-l: to shade, to overshadow, to provide shade-cover. The indefiniteness (tankīr) signals either magnification (too vast to define) or variety (multiple kinds of shading). MASAQ tags NOUN_ABSTRACT, role PREP_OBJ. Canonical variant ẓulal (ظُلَلٍ, plural of ẓulla "pavilion/canopy") shifts from natural shade to constructed covering.

Noun, definite (al-), genitive (majrūr by ʿalā). Plural of arīka. Root ʾ-r-k: to chew (arak-wood), to stay in a place, to recline. An arīka is a couch with a canopy (surīr fī ḥajala), specifically an ornamental seat with a curtained enclosure. All 5 Quranic occurrences appear in paradise contexts with muttakiʾīn. MASAQ tags NOUN_CONCRETE, role PREP_OBJ.

Active participle (ism fāʿil), Form VIII (ittakaʾa), masculine plural nominative. Functions as khabar (predicate) of the nominal sentence whose mubtadaʾ is هُمْ وَأَزْوَٰجُهُمْ. Root w-k-ʾ: to lean, to recline, to support oneself. Form VIII ittakaʾa: to recline, to lean back (on cushions). The active participle signals an ongoing, defining state — not a momentary action but a characteristic posture. All 8 Quranic active participle instances of this root describe paradise or luxury.
Indefinite feminine singular noun, nominative with tanwīn; delayed subject of the first nominal clause after the fronted predicate لَهُمْ فِيهَا.

Indefinite nominative masculine singular noun (gerund/maṣdar). Functions as PRED (predicate) of an implied subject. The tanwīn (-un) marks indefiniteness, giving the peace a quality of boundlessness — not "the peace" (definite, limited) but "a peace" (unbounded). The alif maqṣūra after the lām represents the long ā vowel.

Indefinite accusative masculine singular noun (gerund/maṣdar). Functions as COGN (cognate accusative / mafʿūl muṭlaq) — reinforcing an implied verb of saying. The accusative case (-an) marks it as dependent on the implied verbal action. The tanwīn indicates indefiniteness: not "the word" but "a word" — singular, specific yet unbounded.

Indefinite genitive masculine singular noun. Functions as PREP_OBJ (object of preposition min). The genitive case is governed by min. The tanwīn (-in) marks indefiniteness. The rāʾ carries shadda due to the gemination inherent in the root r-b-b (doubled final radical). The word rabb denotes one who owns, sustains, nurtures, and brings to completion.

Indefinite genitive masculine singular intensive adjective (ṣīghat mubālagha, faʿīl pattern). Functions as ADJ (adjective) modifying rabb. The genitive case matches rabb (agreement). The tanwīn (-in) marks indefiniteness. The faʿīl pattern denotes intensity: not merely "merciful" but "intensely, overwhelmingly, continuously merciful."

Active participle (اسم فاعل, ism fāʿil), Form IV (أَجْرَمَ, ajrama), masculine plural nominative (مرفوع, marfūʿ) with the article الـ (al-). Functions as APPOS (apposition) to the implied vocative noun أَيُّ. Form IV (أَفْعَلَ) is causative/intensive: "one who commits a crime, one who earns guilt." The nominative case is because it is بدل (badal, substitutive apposition) from أَيُّ in the vocative construction. The definite article + active participle = "THE criminals" — a known, defined class, not an indefinite group.
Noun, masculine plural construct (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb) as vocative. From root b-n-y. Construct state governing ādama.
Proper noun (ism 'alam), foreign origin (NOUN_PROP_FOREIGN per MASAQ), genitive by construct (muḍāf ilayhi), triptote declined as diptote.
Definite noun, masculine singular, accusative (object of ta'budū). Root sh-t-n. With definite article al-.
Noun, masculine singular indefinite, nominative (predicate of inna). Root '-d-w. Intensive form (fa'ūl pattern) indicating deep-seated enmity.
Active participle (ism fā'il), Form IV (af'ala → muf'il), masculine singular indefinite, nominative (second predicate of inna or adjective of 'aduww). Root b-y-n.

Indefinite noun, nominative case (مرفوع, marfūʿ), functioning as predicate (خبر, khabar) of the nominal sentence. The nominative -un marks it as the information being predicated about hādhā. The indefinite form (no al-) parallels 36:4 (ṣirāṭin mustaqīmin, genitive) — both are indefinite, contrasting with the definite aṣ-ṣirāṭa of 1:6.

Active participle (اسم فاعل, ism fāʿil) of Form X (istaqāma), indefinite nominative (مرفوع, marfūʿ), functioning as adjective (نعت, naʿt) for ṣirāṭun. Form X istafʿala adds reflexive-estimative force to root q-w-m (to stand): "that which seeks to establish itself upright." Active participle indicates ongoing dynamic state. The nominative -un agrees with ṣirāṭun in case, gender, number, and definiteness (both indefinite).

Indefinite nominative qualitative adjective or predicate on faʿīl pattern. It describes the human as one characterized by dispute, litigation, or adversarial argument.
Indefinite nominative active participle from Form IV abāna/yubīnu. It can modify خَصِيمٌ or function as a second predicate; it allows both intransitive clear and transitive making clear.

Noun (ism) in the accusative indefinite (manṣūb, munakkar) as the direct object of ḍaraba. The indefiniteness (tanwīn) emphasizes the generic nature — "a certain example" or "some kind of argument." The phrase ḍaraba mathalan is idiomatic in the Quran.

Verbal noun (maṣdar / gerund) in the accusative as direct object of nasiya. With possessive pronoun هُ (hū) referring back to the denier — "his own creation," i.e., the fact that he himself was created. The word carries dual meaning: the ACT of creation (process) and the PRODUCT of creation (the created form).

Noun (ism), definite with al-, accusative (manṣūb) as direct object of yuḥyī. Plural of ʿaẓm (bone). The root ʿ-ẓ-m carries dual meaning: "bone" (concrete) and "great/mighty" (abstract). The definite article al- makes this generic: "the bones" = bones in general as a category.

Adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha / qualitative adjective) on the pattern faʿīl, nominative (marfūʿ) as predicate (khabar) of the nominal clause hiya ramīm. Definite adjective (ṣifa) in genitive, agreeing with al-shajar in definiteness, case (genitive), and gender (masculine, since shajar is masculine collective). Pattern afʿal (elative/color pattern) — indicates the quality of greenness.

Feminine plural active participle (ism fā'il) from ṣ-l-ḥ, definite with al-, genitive/accusative case (as object of 'amilū, but the feminine sound plural -āt has -i ending in both). The participle is used substantively: "the sound/fitting [things]." The definite article al- presupposes a known category — the audience is expected to know what "the ṣāliḥāt" are.

Indefinite nominative gerund/noun (maṣdar), serving as the subject of the deleted predicate in the nominal sentence (lahum ajrun = "for them [there is] a reward"). The tanwīn indicates indefiniteness — not "the reward" but "a reward," implying unquantified magnitude. The root '-j-r carries both divine recompense and commercial wage senses.

Nominative abstract noun functioning as an adjective (ṣifa) modifying ajrun. In construct state (muḍāf) with mamnūn as muḍāf ilayhi. The word negates the quality of mamnūn — "a reward [that is] other-than-mamnūn." The root gh-y-r itself carries a fundamental concept of otherness, change, and alteration.

Passive participle (ism maf'ūl) from m-n-n, indefinite genitive (governed by construct with ghayru). The root m-n-n carries two sharply distinct meanings: (1) to cut, to sever, to interrupt; (2) to confer a favor and then reproach the recipient for it (mann). The passive participle preserves BOTH senses: mamnūn = "that which is cut off" AND "that which is reproached/diminished by reminder." ghayru mamnūn therefore means BOTH "never cut off" AND "never accompanied by reproach."
NOUN_ABSTRACT, masculine singular, genitive (majrūr by bi-); definite with al-; the object-of-denial in the yukadhdhibu bi- construction; PREP_OBJ role

Proper noun, nominative case (ism laysa — subject of laysa). The definite proper name for God, from root ʾ-l-h (to worship, to be bewildered/confounded). Nominative -u marks it as the subject of the laysa clause.

Superlative/elative adjective (ism tafḍīl) on the pattern ʾafʿal, from root ḥ-k-m. Genitive case governed by the preposition bāʾ. Functions as the first term of an iḍāfa with al-ḥākimīn. The superlative asserts unsurpassable degree.

Masculine plural active participle (ism fāʿil) from ḥ-k-m, with definite article al-. Genitive case as second term of iḍāfa with ʾaḥkam. The active participle denotes habitual/ongoing agents of judgment. The plural establishes a class from which God is distinguished as supreme.
Noun, masculine singular, genitive (governed by bi), in construct (muḍāf) with rabbika; alif al-waṣl elides in continuous reading (bismi-rabbika); root s-m-w yields ism = name, mark, sign, elevation

Noun in genitive (majrur), second term of idafa with ism. The attached pronoun -ka (2nd person masculine singular) creates a direct address. Root r-b-b denotes nurturing, raising, bringing to maturity.
Definite accusative noun functioning as direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of khalaqa. The definite article al- marks the species generically — "the human" as a category, not a specific individual.
Indefinite genitive noun (majrūr by min). The indefinite form (no article, with tanwīn) generalizes: not "the specific clot" but "clinging matter" as a category. Singular or collective noun.
Noun rabb in nominative (marfu') functioning as mubtada' (subject) of the nominal clause, with 2nd person masculine singular possessive pronoun -ka. Construct state (idafa) with the pronoun.

Elative/superlative adjective (ism tafdil, af'al al-tafdil pattern), definite with al-, nominative (marfu') functioning as khabar (predicate) of rabbuka. The pattern af'alu with al- indicates absolute superlative: "the most generous of all" with no comparison group specified.

Prepositional phrase: bāʾ al-āliyya (instrumental preposition) + definite noun in genitive (majrūr); the preposition marks the means through which teaching occurs; the definite article al- can signal a specific pen (the Primordial Pen) or the genus of writing instruments

Form II (fa''ala) perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, active voice. Doubly transitive: first object = al-insāna (the human), second object = mā lam ya'lam (what he did not know). The Form II causative transforms 'alima (to know) into 'allama (to cause to know / to teach).

Definite noun, accusative case (manṣūb) functioning as the first direct object of 'allama. The definite article al- makes this generic — referring to the human species, not a specific individual. The alif-lām-sād-alif-nūn spelling with alif maqṣūra (ٰ) is the standard Quranic orthography.

Definite noun (maʿrifa), concrete (NOUN_CONCRETE), accusative (manṣūb) — functioning as ism of inna (subject of the emphatic construction). The definite article al- with a genus noun denotes the species generically (al-jins): 'the human being' as a category, not a specific individual.
Noun (ism), genitive case (majrūr) governed by ilā. Construct state (muḍāf) with attached 2nd person masculine singular pronoun -ka (muḍāf ilayhi). Role: PREP_OBJ (prepositional object).

Verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund) on the fu'lā pattern, definite with al-, functioning as the subject (ism) of inna in the accusative. The fu'lā pattern is an intensive maṣdar form — not merely 'a return' but 'THE consummate return.' The alif maqṣūra ending is a feminine marker typical of fu'lā-pattern nouns.

Indefinite accusative noun (manṣūb, tanwīn fatḥa), singular masculine. Functions as the direct object (maf'ūl bihi) of يَنْهَىٰ (yanhā) in the preceding ayah 96:9. The indefinite form conveys generality — not a specific slave but any slave/servant.

Definite verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund), genitive case (majrūr) governed by عَلَى. The definite article (ال) makes this THE guidance — specific, identifiable, not a generic notion. The alif maqṣūra (ى) ending is the standard form of this verbal noun. In the PREP_OBJ role (22 of 92 gerund occurrences) — guidance as object of a preposition is a well-attested pattern.

Preposition بِ (bāʾ al-taʿdiya, transitivizing) + definite verbal noun (maṣdar from Form VIII ittaqā) in genitive; bi- makes taqwā the content-complement of amara — "he commanded [adherence to] protective awareness"; the definite article universalizes: THE taqwā, the known concept

Proper noun (ism 'alam), accusative case (manṣūb) — subject (ism) of أَنَّ, which governs its subject in the accusative. The definite article assimilated into the lām of the divine name. Functions as the agent of the seeing expressed by يَرَىٰ.

Definite noun, feminine singular, genitive case (governed by bi-). Active participle pattern (fā'ila) from n-ṣ-y. The definite article al- + singular = specific forelock (of the person described in 96:9-14). Continued in 96:16 with the appositive nāṣiyatin kādhibatin khāṭi'atin (a lying, sinning forelock).

Indefinite noun, genitive case (majrūr with tanwīn), functioning as badal (substitute appositive) for al-nāṣiya in 96:15. The fā'ila pattern from n-s-y. Appositive relationship: the definite noun of 96:15 is re-stated here indefinitely to receive qualitative adjectives.

Indefinite active participle (ism fā'il), fā'ila pattern (feminine), genitive case with tanwīn, functioning as an adjective (ṣifa) modifying nāṣiya. Attributes the act of lying to the forelock itself, personifying the body part as an agent of deception.

Indefinite active participle (ism fā'il), fā'ila pattern (feminine), genitive case with tanwīn, functioning as a second adjective (ṣifa) modifying nāṣiya. The hamza in khāṭiʾa is from root kh-ṭ-ʾ (with hamza), distinguishing it from kh-ṭ-w (stepping). Attributes moral transgression to the forelock as a second active quality alongside lying.

Accusative singular (manṣūb) definite noun with 3rd person masculine singular possessive pronoun -hu. Active participle pattern (fā'il→nādī) used as a concrete noun denoting a place of assembly. Functions as direct object (maf'ūl bihi) of يَدْعُ. The form nādī literally means "the place where people call out / gather to converse."

Definite noun (al- + zabāniya), accusative case (manṣūb, functioning as direct object of nad'u). Morphological pattern: fu'āliya or fa'āniya — a broken plural form. This is a hapax legomenon in the Quran: the word appears only here in 96:18.
