elative/comparative noun (afʿal pattern: sharr < asharr), nominative as khabar of ulāʾika, construct state before al-bariyya
relative noun (nisba form), genitive (second term of iḍāfa with sharr), definite
noun (active participle used as noun), feminine plural, genitive (following object position), definite with al-
adjective (elative/comparative, afʿalu pattern), nominative as khabar (predicate), first term of iḍāfa
noun (relative adjective/nisba form), feminine singular used collectively, genitive as muḍāf ilayh in iḍāfa with khayru
nominative masculine noun (gerund/maṣdar) + 3rd person masculine plural possessive pronoun; subject of equative nominal sentence
genitive masculine noun + 3rd person masculine plural possessive pronoun; governed by ʿinda (iḍāfa)
nominative feminine plural noun; predicate of the equative nominal sentence (jazāʾuhum = jannātu)
genitive masculine noun (proper noun in MASAQ); second term of iḍāfa with jannātu
genitive noun (ẓarf makān) + 3rd person feminine singular pronoun (referring to jannāt); governed by min
nominative masculine plural noun with definite article; subject of tajrī (delayed subject after verb)
accusative masculine plural active participle; ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) describing the inhabitants of the gardens
nominative proper noun; subject (agent) of raḍiya
accusative masculine noun + 3rd person masculine singular pronoun; direct object of khashiya
definite noun, nominative (marfūʿ), passive subject (nāʾib al-fāʿil) of zulzilat
verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund), accusative (manṣūb), cognate accusative (mafʿūl muṭlaq) of zulzilat; possessive pronoun -hā refers back to al-arḍ
noun, concrete, definite (al-), nominative (ḍamma), feminine, agent/subject of akhrajat
noun, concrete, plural (af'āl pattern), accusative (fatḥa), possessive pronoun -hā (3fs), object of akhrajat
definite noun, nominative singular, concrete noun, agent role
accusative adverbial of time (ẓarf zamān), tanwīn on idh indicating unspecified past reference compressed into future projection
accusative plural noun (akhbār, broken plural of khabar) + feminine singular possessive pronoun -hā referring to al-arḍ; direct object of tuḥaddithu
accusative noun (ism ʾanna) + second-person masculine singular possessive pronoun -ka; subject of the ʾanna clause
noun, adverbial accusative of time, annexed to idhin (then), nunated tanwīn indicating indefinite subordinate clause
noun, definite with al-, nominative (marfūʿ), subject (fāʿil) of yaṣduru
noun, plural of shattā or shatīt, accusative (manṣūb), ḥāl (circumstantial adverb) describing state of al-nās, nunated (indefinite)
noun, plural of ʿamal, accusative (manṣūb), object of yuraw, with 3rd person masculine plural possessive pronoun -hum
noun of instrument (mifʿāl pattern), accusative (manṣūb) as direct object of yaʿmal, first term of iḍāfa with dharratin
noun, genitive (majrūr) by iḍāfa to mithqāla, nunated (indefinite), singular
gerund/masdar, accusative (manṣūb) as tamyīz (specification) clarifying the nature of the mithqāl, nunated indefinite
noun of instrument (mīm prefix), accusative as direct object of yaʿmal; first term of iḍāfah with dharrah
noun, genitive (kasrah + tanwīn) in iḍāfah with mithqāl; indefinite
noun/masdar, accusative of specification (tamyīz) distinguishing the type of action; indefinite

Feminine plural active participle (ism fā'il) from '-d-w, definite with al-, genitive case governed by oath-وَ. Form I participle عَادِي ('ādī) with feminine sound plural -āt suffix, yielding العاديات. The genitive ending -i reflects jarr by the oath particle.

Indefinite accusative gerund (maṣdar), functioning either as مَفْعُول مُطْلَق (maf'ūl muṭlaq, cognate accusative describing the manner of the action) or as حَال (ḥāl, circumstantial accusative describing the state of the 'ādiyāt). The tanwīn -an confirms the indefinite accusative.
Active participle (ism fa'il), Form IV (af'ala → muf'il), feminine plural, definite with al-, genitive case (after oath particle). The IV form (awra) is causative: "to cause fire to appear."

Gerund (masdar), indefinite accusative, functioning as maf'ul mutlaq (cognate accusative) — intensifying the action described by al-muriyat. The accusative case marks it as an adverbial modifier of manner.

Definite feminine plural active participle (ism fā'il, mu-pattern indicating Form IV), genitive case (majrūr) governed by the oath particle wa- from 100:1. Form IV of gh-w-r: aghāra / yughīru = to raid, to descend suddenly upon. The feminine plural -āt suffix can refer to horses (khayl, grammatically feminine), mares specifically, or any feminine plural entities. MASAQ maps this to gh-y-r (to change), but classical grammarians unanimously derive مُغِيرَات from gh-w-r (to raid/descend). The Form IV active participle mu-pattern (مُفْعِل) from gh-w-r yields mughīr; from gh-y-r it would yield mughīr as well (since both have identical Form IV conjugation), but the semantic fields diverge completely.
Indefinite accusative noun (masdar/concrete noun). Direct object of atharna. Hapax legomenon — this is the ONLY occurrence of this root in the entire Quran.
Verbal noun (masdar/gerund) in the indefinite accusative. Functions as the direct object of wasatna. The tanwin (-an) marks indefiniteness, suggesting an unspecified gathering.

Definite noun in the accusative (manṣūb) as ism of inna (the subject of the emphatic clause). The definite article al- is for al-jins (generic reference) — referring to the human species as a whole, not a specific individual. The alif-lām-nūn-sīn-alif-nūn form (insān) is the standard Quranic noun for "the human being."

Noun رَبّ (rabb, nurturer/lord) in genitive as object of preposition + possessive pronoun ـهِۦ (hi, his) referring back to al-insān; the prepositional phrase functions as a fronted qualifier (muqaddam) before the predicate la-kanūdun

Predicate (khabar) of inna in the nominative (marfū'). The fa'ūl pattern (kanūd) is an intensive/persistent adjective form indicating a deep-seated, habitual quality — not occasional ingratitude but a defining characteristic.

Noun (ism), masculine singular, indefinite, nominative (marfūʿ) as predicate of inna (khabar inna). Pattern faʿīl (فَعِيل), an intensive/habitual adjective denoting one characterized by the quality of witnessing. The indefinite form (shahīdun, not ash-shahīdu) makes the predication qualitative: "he is [a type of being characterized as] witness" rather than "he is THE witness."

Preposition prefixed to hubbi. Governs the genitive case. Ambiguous function: (a) lam al-ta'lil — causative: "because of / due to," (b) lam al-takhsis — specificative: "with respect to / in the matter of," (c) lam al-jarr — directional: "for / toward."
Verbal noun (masdar/gerund) in the genitive case, governed by li-. First element of an idafa (construct) with al-khayri. From root h-b-b. The GERUND form indicates the abstract concept of loving.
Noun (abstract) in the genitive case, second element of idafa with hubb. Definite article al- indicates the generic concept ("the good" / "wealth" in general). From root kh-y-r.

Lām al-tawkid (al-ibtidā'/al-muzaḥlaqa, "sliding lām") prefixed to the predicate (khabar) of inna, completing the inna...la- double-emphasis frame, + qualitative adjective (sifat mushabbaha) of pattern fa'īl from geminate root sh-d-d in nominative case (-un) as khabar inna
Definite noun, plural of qabr, genitive case governed by fi. The definite article al- indicates all graves universally, not specific ones.

Noun, masculine plural (jam' taksīr — broken plural of ṣadr), definite with al-, genitive (majrūr) governed by fī. The broken plural pattern fu'ūl indicates concrete plurality. ṣadr literally means "front, forepart, chest, breast" — the seat of thought, emotion, intention in Quranic anthropology. The definite article al- here is for generic reference (istighrāq) — ALL chests, not specific ones.

Noun (ism), masculine singular, accusative (manṣūb) as ism inna. Attached pronoun -hum (3rd person masculine plural, genitive) functions as muḍāf ilayh in a possessive construct. rabb is a noun of agency (quasi-participle) from r-b-b, pattern fa'l. The accusative case is governed by inna.

Noun (ism), masculine singular, accusative (manṣūb) as adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). Composed of yawm (day) + idh (when, at the time of) + tanwīn (nunation replacing the genitive iḍāfa clause). The tanwīn on idhin is compensatory (ʿiwaḍ) — replacing an elided clause (the events described in 100:9-10: when graves are overturned and what is in breasts is obtained). The accusative marks temporal adverbial function.
Adjective, intensive form (ṣīghat al-mubālagha), pattern faʿīl (فَعِيل), masculine singular, nominative (marfūʿ) as khabar inna (predicate of inna)

Definite noun, feminine singular, nominative (marfūʿ) — functioning as mubtadaʾ (subject) with elided khabar (predicate). Morphologically: al- (definite article) + qāriʿa (active participle, fāʿila pattern, feminine of fāʿil from Form I qaraʿa). The fāʿila form denotes an active agent — "the one [feminine] that strikes." Used as a proper noun (NOUN_PROP in MASAQ) to name the eschatological event. The feminine form may reflect agreement with an implied feminine noun (sāʿa "hour," wāqiʿa "event," qiyāma "rising") or may be an independent feminine agent designation.

Definite active participle (ism fā'il) from qara'a (I), feminine singular with tā' marbūṭa, nominative (marfū') as khabar (predicate) of the nominal sentence. Functions as a proper noun (ism 'alam) for the eschatological event — the definite article marks it as a unique, known entity. The active participle form indicates an ongoing or characteristic action: not "the one that struck" (past) but "the one that strikes" — the striker by nature.

Active participle (ism fa'il) from Form I, feminine singular with definite article al-. Nominative case (marfu') as mubtada' mu'akhkhar (delayed subject) of the nominal sentence ma l-qari'atu. The ta' marbuta feminine ending creates the sense of an abstract force, not a specific actor.

Noun (ism jins jamʿī), masculine, definite with al-, nominative (marfūʿ) as the subject (fāʿil) of yakūnu. an-nās is a collective noun referring to humanity as a whole, not a specific group. The definite article al- gives it generic reference: "humankind [as a species]."

Noun, masculine singular used collectively, definite (al-), genitive (governed by كَ). farāsh from root f-r-sh originally means "what is spread" — applied to both moths/butterflies (creatures that spread their wings) and bed-spreads/coverings (things spread on the ground). The definite article al- makes the simile specific.

Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) from Form I of b-th-th, masculine singular, definite with al-, genitive (majrūr) as an adjective (ṣifa) modifying al-farāsh. The passive voice indicates that the scattering is done TO the moths/people — they are scattered by an external force, not scattering themselves. The reduplicated root (b-th-th, where the second and third radicals are identical) phonetically enacts the scattering: the repeated "th" sound mimics dispersal.
Definite noun, broken plural of jabal, nominative (marfu') as subject of takunu. The definite article al- marks the generic/universal: ALL mountains, not specific ones.

Prefixed PREP كَ (harf al-tashbih — particle of comparison/simile) governing the definite noun ٱلْعِهْنِ in genitive (majrur); the noun is first element of a genitive-adjective chain with al-manfushi following, all serving as the predicate of takunu in the preceding clause
Definite passive participle (ism al-maf'ul) from Form I nafasha, genitive (majrur) agreeing with al-'ihni as an adjective. Describes the state of the wool as having been actively processed/dispersed.

Noun of instrument (ism al-ala); broken plural mawazin of mizan; pattern mafa'il from mif'al; nominative case (marfu') as subject (fa'il) of thaqulat; possessive pronoun -hu (3ms) attached; the plural form suggests multiple scales or multiple acts of weighing

Verbal noun / gerund (maṣdar, pattern fi'la), feminine singular, indefinite (nakira), genitive (majrūr) governed by fī. The tanwīn (nunation) marks indefiniteness — "A life" (any/some life), not "THE life." The pattern fi'la (فِعْلَة) denotes a single instance or a specific mode of the root action: not "living" in general but "a particular manner of living, a specific life-experience."

Active participle (ism fā'il), feminine singular (matching 'īsha), indefinite (nakira), genitive (majrūr) as attributive adjective (na't/ṣifa) for 'īshatin. The ACTIVE participle form is grammatically crucial: it makes 'īsha the AGENT of satisfaction — the life ITSELF is satisfied/pleased, not passively made pleasant. Compare with the passive participle marḍiyya ("approved, found satisfactory by another") in 89:28. Pattern fā'ila (فَاعِلَة) = the one who performs the action of r-ḍ-y.

Noun of instrument (ism āla) in the plural form mawāzīn (pattern mafā'īl), nominative case (marfū') as fā'il (subject) of khaffat. The possessive pronoun -hū (his) refers back to man. mawāzīn is the broken plural of mīzān (مِيزَان, pattern mīfāl / mif'āl — instrument for w-z-n). The nominative case marks it as the agent: it is the scales themselves that are described as light, not the person directly. This grammatical structure makes the evaluation impersonal — the instrument reports a result.

Noun, feminine singular, nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject) of the nominal sentence. With attached pronoun -hu (3rd person masculine singular, genitive — possessive). The noun umm is from root '-m-m and carries a remarkably wide semantic range: mother (biological), origin/source (umm al-kitāb), shelter/abode (the mother as refuge), head/brain (umm al-raʾs), foundation/matrix (umm al-qurā). The form is the basic fa'l pattern (CvCC) with the doubled final consonant (umm from *'umm).

Noun / active participle (ism fāʿil), feminine singular with tāʾ marbūṭa, nominative (marfūʿ) as khabar (predicate) of the nominal sentence whose mubtadaʾ is ummuhu. From root h-w-y on the pattern fāʿila (active participle of Form I hawā/yahwī). The tanwīn indicates either indefiniteness (a hāwiya — a plunging thing) or proper-noun tanwīn (Hāwiya as a name, like ʿArafātun). As active participle, it preserves verbal force: "one that is [currently/continuously] falling."
Indefinite nominative noun (ism marfu' munakkar). Functions as predicate (khabar) answering ma hiyah (101:10), or as mubtada with hamiyatun as khabar. Feminine noun.
Feminine active participle (ism fa'il mu'annath) from Form I (hamiya/yahma), nominative indefinite. Functions as adjective (na't/sifa) modifying nar, or as khabar (predicate) if nar is mubtada.

Definite masdar (verbal noun) of Form VI (tafa'ula), nominative case, functioning as the subject (fa'il) of alhakum. The definite article al- indicates a known, specific phenomenon. Form VI (tafa'ula) indicates reciprocal/mutual action: competing WITH EACH OTHER in accumulation.
Definite noun, plural of maqbara (place noun pattern maf'ala), accusative (mansub) as the direct object of zurtumu. The pattern maf'ala/maf'il indicates a place or time of the root action.

Verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund), masculine singular, accusative (manṣūb) as cognate accusative (mafʿūl muṭlaq) qualifying the verb taʿlamūna. It is also the first element (muḍāf) of an iḍāfa construct with al-yaqīn. The dual grammatical role — mafʿūl muṭlaq to the verb AND muḍāf to yaqīn — creates a layered structure: it is simultaneously the intensifier of the verb and the container qualified by its content (certainty).

Verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund), masculine singular, definite (with al-), genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayh in the iḍāfa construct ʿilma l-yaqīni. The definite article al- makes this "THE certainty" — not generic certainty but a specific, absolute certainty (al-yaqīn al-maʿhūd — the well-known certainty).

Noun (ism), masculine singular, definite with al- (harf at-taʿrīf), accusative (manṣūb) as direct object (mafʿūl bih) of la-tarawunna. Pattern faʿīl (فَعِيل) — an intensive noun form denoting the quality in its extreme degree. jaḥīm is used as both a common noun ("fierce fire, blazing heat") and a proper noun (one of the Quranic names for the eschatological fire). The definite article here can indicate: (1) the well-known jaḥīm (ʿahd dhihnī — mentally known referent), (2) the generic category of jaḥīm (jins), or (3) a unique, specific entity (ʿahd ḥaḍūrī).

Noun, accusative singular (mansūb), in the status constructus (iḍāfa) with al-yaqīni. Functions as adverbial accusative (ḥāl or mafʿūl muṭlaq) — "seeing it [as/with] the eye of certainty." The accusative case marks it as modifying the verb la-tarawunnahā: it specifies the MODE or MANNER of seeing. The MASAQ tag NOUN_ABSTRACT with role ADJ indicates it qualifies the seeing action. The word is semantically polyvalent: ʿayn means "eye" (organ), "essence/self" (ʿaynuhū = he himself), "spring/source" (of water), "spy/observer," and "gold coin" (ʿayn = cash money in classical Arabic). Each meaning generates a different reading of the phrase.

Definite noun, genitive singular (majrūr) — second term of the iḍāfa construction ʿayna l-yaqīni. The genitive case is governed by the construct state with ʿayn. Morphologically: al- (definite article) + yaqīn (verbal noun/gerund from Form I yaqina, faʿīl pattern = active intensity). The faʿīl pattern indicates an inherent, intensive quality — yaqīn is not merely "being certain" but "that which IS certainty itself." The definite article al- marks this as THE certainty — absolute, specific, known.

Compound temporal adverb: yawma (accusative, adverbial) + idhin (then, at that time). The tanwin on idhin is 'iwad tanwin — compensating for an omitted clause (idh kadha wa-kadha = "when such-and-such happened"). The accusative marks it as an adverbial of time (maf'ul fihi / zarf zaman). Refers to the eschatological Day established in the surah's prior context.

Definite noun in the genitive case (majrur by 'an). Morphologically a masdar/gerund (fa'il pattern: na'im) from na'ima (to be in ease, to live comfortably). The definite article al- makes this UNIVERSAL — not "some pleasures" but THE totality of ease/comfort. Pattern na'im (فعيل) is an intensive adjective-turned-noun, suggesting a state that is deeply, thoroughly embedded.

Definite noun, masculine singular, genitive (majrūr) — governed by the oath particle وَ. Morphologically: al- (definite article) + ʿaṣr (verbal noun / noun of time from Form I ʿaṣara). MASAQ classifies this as NOUN_ABSTRACT with syntactic role PREP_OBJ (object of the oath preposition). The genitive -i ending reflects subordination to the oath particle. The definite article indicates totality — not an era or a pressing, but THE era, THE pressing.

Definite concrete noun (ism ma'rifa), accusative (manṣūb) as ism inna. The alif-lām is al-jinsiyya (generic article) — it refers to the entire human species, not a particular individual. The accusative case is governed by inna. Morphologically: in-s-ān, a fa'lān pattern from '-n-s, suggesting a being characterized by the root quality (sociability/intimacy). The long ā in -ān can indicate intensity or habituality.

Indefinite gerund (maṣdar), genitive (majrūr) governed by fī. The indefiniteness (tankīr) serves rhetorical amplification: not "the loss" (a defined, bounded loss) but "a loss" — unquantified, unbounded, vast. Classical grammarians note three possible functions of tankīr here: li-l-ta'ẓīm (magnification: "a tremendous loss"), li-l-tahwīl (terrification: "a horrifying loss"), li-l-ibhām (vagueness: "a loss beyond specification"). The kasra ending (-in) marks the genitive case under fī's governance.

Active participle (ism fa'il) from Form I, feminine plural with definite article al-. Accusative case (mansub) as direct object (maf'ul bihi) of 'amilu. The feminine plural -at form indicates abstract actions/qualities rather than specific actors.

Prefixed PREP بِ (harf al-jarr — instrument/content/accompaniment) governing the definite verbal noun (masdar/gerund) ٱلْحَقِّ in genitive (majrur); functions as PREP_OBJ specifying the content/instrument of the mutual charging (tawassaw) — "they charged each other WITH truth"

Prefixed PREP بِ (harf al-jarr — instrument/content) governing the definite verbal noun (masdar/gerund) ٱلصَّبْرِ in genitive (majrur); functions as PREP_OBJ specifying the content/instrument of the second mutual charging (tawassaw) — parallel to bi-l-haqq in word 9–10

Indefinite noun, masculine singular, nominative (marfu') — functioning as mubtada (subject) in a nominal sentence with the prepositional phrase li-kulli... as khabar. The indefiniteness (tankir) is rhetorically marked: had it been al-waylu (definite), it would point to a specific, known woe; the indefinite form leaves the nature and extent of the woe unspecified, creating open-ended dread. NOUN_ABSTRACT in MASAQ, role SUBJ.

Prefixed PREP لِ (harf al-jarr — here lām al-ikhtiṣāṣ specifying dedication, or lām al-istiḥqāq marking deservingness) governing the indefinite noun كُلِّ in genitive (majrur); kulli serves as muḍāf (first term of iḍāfa/construct) with the following humazatin as muḍāf ilayhi, universalizing the address — every instance of the described behavior, none excluded

Indefinite noun/intensive adjective, masculine form used generically (not gender-specific), singular, genitive (majrur) — governed by kulli as mudaf ilayhi. Morphological pattern fu'ala (فُعَلة) which denotes habitual, intensive agency. The ta marbuta does NOT mark feminine gender here — it marks intensification (like 'allama, rahhala, nassaba). ADJ_INTENS in MASAQ, role GEN_CONS.

Indefinite noun/intensive adjective, masculine form used generically, singular, genitive (majrur) — in apposition (badal or 'atf bayan) to humazatin. Same fu'ala (فُعَلة) intensive pattern. ADJ_INTENS in MASAQ, role APPOS. The apposition means lumaza is a SECOND DESCRIPTION of the same person as humaza — not a separate individual but an overlapping characterization.
Indefinite accusative noun (ism mankir mansub). Direct object of jama'a. The indefiniteness (tanwin) generalizes: not "the wealth" but "a/any wealth" — maximizing scope.

Noun, accusative (governed by anna as its subject in the anna-clause — ism anna). Concrete noun with possessive pronoun -hū (his). Functions as the subject of the predicate akhladahū within the anna-clause. The accusative marking is required by anna, not by verbal government.

Definite noun, genitive case (governed by fī), feminine. Morphological pattern fu'alah — an intensive/exaggerative form (ṣīghat al-mubālaghah) indicating an entity that crushes excessively/repeatedly. Used as a proper name (ism 'alam) for a specific entity, defined in the following ayah (104:5).
Definite noun on the fu'alah pattern (intensive/hyperbolic form). Nominative case (marfu') as predicate of the nominal sentence "ma l-hutamatu." The alif-lam (al-) indicates a known/specific entity.
Noun, feminine, nominative (raf') as predicate (khabar) of the implied subject al-ḥuṭamah from 104:5. First element of iḍāfa with Allāh, hence no tanwīn. Definite through iḍāfa.
Proper noun, genitive (jarr) as second element of iḍāfa (nāru llāhi). The kasra on the hā' marks genitive case governed by the iḍāfa construction.

Passive participle (ism al-maf'ūl), feminine, nominative, definite with al-. Pattern mu-fʿal-a from Form IV (awqada). Functions as an adjective (ṣifa) modifying nāru. Follows the iḍāfa nāru llāhi as a post-iḍāfa attributive — grammatically modifying the first element of the iḍāfa (nāru).

Definite noun, feminine plural (broken plural of fuʾād), genitive (majrūr) — governed by the preposition ʿalā. The pattern afʿida is a broken plural of fuʿāl (fuʾād → afʾida). al-afʾida refers to the plural of fuʾād — not the physical heart (qalb) but the innermost cognitive-emotional core. In MASAQ: NOUN_ABSTRACT with PREP_OBJ role (object of the preposition). The definite article al- indicates universality: THE hearts, i.e., all hearts — not specific individuals but the category of inner cores.

Passive participle (ism maf'ul), feminine singular, indefinite (tanwin), from the root '-s-d. Pattern: mu-f-'al-a (muf'ala). Functions as the predicate (khabar) of inna. Describes the state of being sealed or closed, not the act of sealing — the closure is complete and permanent.

Noun (ism), indefinite genitive (majrūr bi-fī), plural of ʿamūd (عَمُود). The broken plural ʿamad (فَعَل pattern) denotes multiple pillars/columns. Indefinite form (no al-) universalizes the image — not specific pillars but an unspecified multiplicity.

Passive participle (ism mafʿūl), Form II (tafʿīl → mufaʿʿal), feminine singular indefinite genitive. Modifies ʿamadin as an adjective (ṣifa). Form II's doubling of the middle radical intensifies the base meaning: not merely "stretched" but "stretched out extensively, repeatedly, deliberately." The passive voice implies an agent who performs the extending.
Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE) in nominative case (marfu') as subject (fa'il) of fa'ala; with 2nd person masculine singular possessive pronoun -ka; definite through idafa (construct state with pronoun)
Noun (active participle pattern, NOUN_ACTIVE_PART) in genitive case (majrur) due to bi- preposition; plural of sahib; in construct state (idafa) with al-fil

Noun (NOUN_CONCRETE) in genitive case (majrur) due to idafa (construct state) with ashabi; definite with the article al-; this is the ONLY occurrence of this root in the entire Quran (hapax legomenon)

Form I verbal noun (maṣdar/gerund) كَيْد in accusative case (manṣūb) as direct object of yajʿal; in iḍāfa with attached 3rd person masculine plural possessive pronoun -hum referring to the People of the Elephant (Aṣḥāb al-Fīl) of 105:1

Verbal noun (masdar) of Form II (taf'il pattern), genitive case (majrur) governed by fi. Form II adds causative/intensive meaning to the base root: dalla (to go astray) becomes dallala (to cause to go astray, to mislead intensely).

Indefinite accusative noun (concrete), direct object of arsala. The indefinite form (tankir) with -an ending emphasizes the unknown/unspecified nature of these birds — "a kind of birds" rather than "the birds."

Indefinite accusative noun (concrete), functioning as adjective/descriptor (na't) for ṭayran, or as ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) describing the manner of the birds. Broken plural form (taksir cogulu) — the singular is disputed among classical grammarians (ibbīl, ibbawl, or no singular).

Prepositional phrase: inseparable bāʾ al-istiʿāna (instrumental preposition) + indefinite noun in genitive; broken plural of ḥajar (stone) in fiʿāla pattern; tanwīn marks indefiniteness — unspecified quantity of stones; bāʾ introduces the instrument of the verb tarmī (pelting WITH stones)
Noun, indefinite genitive (after kāf of comparison). 'aṣf = dried grain stalks, chaff, straw — the husk remaining after grain has been threshed.

Passive participle (maf'ūl pattern) from root '-k-l, indefinite genitive agreeing with 'aṣf. Functions as an adjective (ṣifa) modifying 'aṣfin. The mīm prefix + passive pattern indicates completed passivity: "having been eaten."

PREP لِ (lām al-taʿlīl / lām al-taʿajjub / lām al-jarr) governing the genitive + Form IV verbal noun (maṣdar of ʾālafa, yuʾlifu) إِيلَاف in genitive case (majrūr); functions as first term (muḍāf) of an iḍāfa with Quraysh; the Form IV pattern (ʾifʿāl with lengthened initial vowel due to hamza-lām sequence) marks CAUSATION ("to cause familiarity") rather than the Form I sense ("to become familiar"); the lām syntactically governs the entire surah, framing what follows as subordinate to a stated purpose; the agent of the ʾīlāf is grammatically unspecified

Proper noun (ism ʿalam), genitive (majrūr) as the second term (muḍāf ilayh) of the iḍāfa ʾīlāf Quraysh. Takes tanwīn (nunation: -in), which is unusual for proper nouns — most Arabic proper nouns are diptotic (mamnūʿ min aṣ-ṣarf) and do not take tanwīn. Quraysh taking tanwīn suggests it is treated as a triptotic noun (munṣarif), possibly because it was originally a common noun (diminutive form quraysh from qarsh) that became a tribal name. The diminutive form (fuʿayl pattern) suggests either endearment ("little gatherer") or belittlement.
Verbal noun (masdar) of Form IV (if'al), genitive case as appositive (badal) to ilaf in 106:1, with 3rd person masculine plural possessive suffix -him. Functions as the head of the nominal clause.

Verbal noun (masdar/gerund), singular feminine, accusative case functioning as the direct object (maf'ul bihi) of ilafihim or as accusative of specification (tamyiz). First element of a construct (idafa) with al-shita'i.
Noun, definite with al-, genitive case as second element of construct (idafa) with rihlata. Hapax legomenon — appears only here in the Quran.
Noun, definite with al-, genitive case coordinated with al-shita'i through wa. Hapax legomenon — appears only here in the Quran.

Noun in accusative (manṣūb) as the direct object (maf'ūl bih) of ya'budū. First element of a complex iḍāfa chain: rabb + hādhā + al-bayt. The accusative marks it as the target of worship. Unlike 1:2 where rabb is in the genitive (apposition to Allāh), here rabb stands independently as the object of the verb — the entity to be worshipped is defined ONLY through its relationship to "this house."

Definite noun in genitive (majrūr) governed by the iḍāfa relationship with rabb (through hādhā). al-bayt with the definite article in Quranic context typically refers to the Ka'ba (al-Bayt al-Harām, al-Bayt al-'Atīq). The genitive case follows from the construct chain.

Verbal noun / gerund (maṣdar), masculine, genitive (majrūr) governed by min. Indefinite (nakira), indicating universal hunger rather than a specific instance. The tanwīn (-in) confirms indefiniteness and genitive case.

Verbal noun / gerund (maṣdar), masculine, genitive (majrūr) governed by min. Indefinite (nakira), universalizing fear beyond any specific threat. The tanwīn (-in) and the ending mīm-like sign (ۭ) confirm indefinite genitive.

PREP بِ (bāʾ al-jarr functioning as content/object marker for kadhdhaba bi- "to deny [something]") governing the genitive + definite noun ٱلدِّين (al- definite article + dīn) in genitive case (majrūr); the bi- is inseparable from the verb's transitivity (kadhdhaba bi-shayʾ = "to deny something") and specifies WHAT is denied; the definite article points to THE established, known dīn — not a dīn but the recognized system

Definite noun (or substantivized adjective, ADJ_QUALIT per MASAQ), masculine singular, accusative (manṣūb) — functioning as the direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of yaduʿʿu. al- (definite article) + yatīm (from root y-t-m). The accusative case marks it as receiving the action of the pushing verb. The definite article al- can be read as: (1) generic/jins — "the orphan" as a class (any orphan), or (2) specific — a particular orphan known to the audience, or (3) ʿahd — "the [previously mentioned/well-known] orphan."

Noun (ism), genitive case (majrūr) after the preposition ʿalā. First term of an iḍāfa (genitive construct) with al-miskīni. The genitive construct ṭaʿāmi l-miskīni is ambiguous: (1) food FOR the destitute (objective genitive — food given to them), (2) food OF the destitute (possessive genitive — food belonging to them, their rightful share), (3) food CHARACTERIZED BY the destitute (descriptive genitive — food associated with poverty). Each reading carries different social implications.

Intensive adjective (ṣīghat al-mubālagha, mifʿīl pattern), genitive case (majrūr) as the second term of the iḍāfa construct ṭaʿāmi l-miskīni. The definite article al- makes this generic: "the destitute one" as a class, not a specific individual. The mifʿīl pattern (miskīn) indicates one deeply characterized by the root quality — not merely "poor" but one whose very being is defined by sukūn (stillness, immobility). The genitive case is governed by the iḍāfa relationship.

Indefinite noun, masculine singular, nominative (marfūʿ with tanwīn). Functions as mubtadaʾ (subject) in a nominal sentence with li-l-muṣallīna as khabar (predicate), or as khabar muqaddam (fronted predicate) with a deleted mubtadaʾ. The tanwīn (nunation) on waylun gives phonetic emphasis and marks indefiniteness — the woe is unquantified, unbounded. NOUN_ABSTRACT in MASAQ, functioning as SUBJ. The word is used 40 times in the Quran, almost always in the formula "waylun li-" (woe to) targeting a group.

Prepositional phrase: lām al-jarr (preposition governing genitive, lām al-ikhtiṣāṣ marking appropriation/designation) + definite active participle, masculine plural, genitive (majrūr). NOUN_ACTIVE_PART from Form II ṣallā/yuṣallī. The lām assigns waylun to its target — the woe belongs to / is designated for these pray-ers. The definite article al- marks them as a known, specific category.

Gerund/verbal noun (maṣdar), genitive case governed by 'an, with 3rd person masculine plural possessive suffix -him. Singular form ṣalāt (not plural ṣalawāt), suggesting a unified concept of prayer rather than individual prayer instances.

Active participle (ism fā'il), Form I, masculine plural nominative. Functions as khabar (predicate) of the nominal sentence hum... sāhūna within the relative clause. Indicates an ongoing, characteristic state — not a momentary lapse but a defining quality.

Definite noun, accusative case (mansub) as the direct object of yamna'una. Pattern maf'ul (passive participle pattern), meaning "what is given as aid" or "what facilitates." The definite article al- generalizes: not "a specific aid" but "aid as a category" -- the entire genus of small social assistance.

Definite noun in the accusative (direct object of a'taynaka). The pattern is fa'wal (كَوْثَر), an intensive/superlative nominal form from the root k-th-r. The definite article al- marks it as either a proper noun or the quintessential instance of abundance. Accusative as second object of the double-transitive verb a'taynaka.

Prepositional phrase: PREP لِ (lām al-ikhtiṣāṣ / lām al-taʿlīl) + NOUN رَبّ in genitive (مجرور) by iḍāfah with 2ms possessive pronoun ـكَ (-ka); lām marks exclusive dedication or purpose — "for your Lord alone"

Active participle (ism fa'il) of Form I fa'ila, with 2nd person masculine singular possessive suffix -ka functioning as the object of the participle. Governed by inna in the accusative (mansub). The active participle indicates a continuous, characteristic state — not a single act of hatred but an ongoing disposition.

Definite elative/comparative adjective (af'al pattern), nominative case as the predicate (khabar) of inna. The definite article al- makes this categorical — not "a cut-off one" but THE cut-off one (the ultimate, definitive instance of being severed).

Active participle (ism fāʿil) of Form I k-f-r, masculine plural (jāmiʿ mudhakkar sālim), nominative (marfūʿ) with -ūna ending as it is the munādā (vocative complement) of yā ayyuhā. The definite article al- is required after ayyuhā. The active participle indicates an ongoing, continuous state — not "those who once covered" but "those who are in a state of covering." As APPOS (appositive) in MASAQ, it serves as the identifying noun in the vocative construction.

Active participle (ism fāʿil), masculine plural nominative (marfūʿ). Pattern fāʿil (فَاعِل) from Form I, with sound masculine plural ending -ūna. Functions as predicate (khabar) of the nominal sentence whose subject is antum. As an active participle, it denotes an ongoing, habitual state — not "you do not worship" (momentary) but "you are not worshippers" (identity). The active participle fāʿil denotes the doer of an action as a permanent characteristic.

Active participle (ism fāʿil) from Form I (faʿala), pattern fāʿil (فَاعِل). Masculine singular, nominative (marfūʿ) with tanwīn as the predicate (khabar) of the nominal sentence whose subject is أَنَا. As an active participle, it expresses an ONGOING STATE or CHARACTERISTIC — not a single act but an abiding quality. The participle functions as a noun of agent: "one who worships / a worshipper."

Active participle (ism fa'il), masculine plural nominative (sound masculine plural -una ending), Form I. Functions as the predicate (khabar) of the nominal sentence whose subject is antum. As an active participle used predicatively, it denotes a permanent, inherent characteristic — "ones who are [by nature] worshippers" — rather than a momentary action.

Noun (ism), NOUN_ABSTRACT from root d-y-n. Nominative case (marfu') as subject of the nominal sentence (mubtada' mu'akhkhar / sonralanmis mubteda). Possessive construct with 2nd person masculine plural suffix -kum.

Noun (ism), NOUN_ABSTRACT from root d-y-n. Nominative case (marfu') as delayed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar) of the second nominal clause. Construct state with elided 1st person singular possessive (ya al-mutakallim) — the -i ending represents both genitive case AND the remnant of the possessive pronoun.

Noun (maṣdar/verbal noun or proper noun), masculine singular, nominative (marfūʿ) as subject (fāʿil) of jāʾa. First term of iḍāfa construct naṣru llāhi — naṣr is muḍāf (annexed), losing its tanwīn. The iḍāfa attributes the aid to God as its source or possessor.

Proper noun (ism ʿalam), masculine, genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayh in the construct naṣru llāhi. God is the possessor/source of the naṣr. The word Allāh is analyzed as al- + ilāh (the deity) with hamza elision and lām assimilation, or alternatively as a primary proper noun.

Gerund/verbal noun (maṣdar), masculine singular, nominative (marfūʿ) as second subject of jāʾa, coordinated with naṣr via wa. Definite with al- (the definite article), suggesting a SPECIFIC, known opening — not any opening but THE opening. In iḍāfa, naṣr loses its tanwīn (naṣru llāhi), but fatḥ carries al- instead, making it independently definite rather than linked to Allāh by iḍāfa. This asymmetry is significant.

Definite noun (al + nās), accusative (manṣūb) as direct object of ra'ayta. Root '-n-s. The definite article al- marks this as the totality of people — not "some people" but "THE people" as a collective. Syntactic role: OBJ.
Noun (ism), genitive (majrūr) governed by fī. First term of an iḍāfa (genitive construct): dīni llāhi = "the dīn OF God." Root d-y-n. Syntactic role: PREP_OBJ (object of preposition).

Proper noun (ism ʿalam), genitive (majrūr) as second term of iḍāfa: dīni llāhi = "the dīn of God." Root '-l-h. The genitive marks possession/attribution: the dīn BELONGS to God. Syntactic role: GEN_CONS (genitive in construct).

Noun (ism), accusative (manṣūb) as ḥāl (circumstantial accusative) describing the manner of entry: "entering [in the state of being] multitudes." Root f-w-j. Broken plural of fawj. The tanwīn (-an) marks it as indefinite accusative. Syntactic role: CIRCUM (circumstantial).

Preposition بِ (ḥarf jarr — bā' al-istiʿāna of instrument / bā' al-muṣāḥaba of accompaniment) + verbal noun (maṣdar) حَمْد masculine singular, genitive (majrūr) governed by bi-, in construct (iḍāfa) with rabbika that follows (objective genitive: "the praise of your Lord"); the bi-maṣdar phrase functions as the instrument/manner of the command sabbiḥ

Noun (ism), masculine singular, genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayh to ḥamdi. The -ka suffix is 2nd person masculine singular possessive pronoun. rabb is in construct state (muḍāf) with the pronoun. From root r-b-b: one who nurtures, raises, owns, sustains, brings to completion stage by stage.

Intensive adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha / ism al-mubālagha), fa''āl pattern, indefinite, accusative (manṣūb) as khabar (predicate) of kāna. From root t-w-b: to return, to turn back. The fa''āl pattern indicates extreme frequency or intensity of the action — one who turns back CONSTANTLY, REPEATEDLY, without ceasing.

Noun, feminine dual (tathnia muʾannath), nominative (marfūʿ) as subject (fāʿil) of tabbat. The dual form yadā (from yad, base form yady) takes the alif ending in the nominative. The tāʾ marbūṭa of tabbat agrees with the feminine gender of yad. As the first element of the iḍāfa chain yadā abī lahabin, it is in the construct state (muḍāf).

Noun, masculine singular, genitive (majrūr) with tanwīn (nunation: -in) as muḍāf ilayh to abī. The tanwīn confirms it is NOT in iḍāfa with anything further — it is the terminal noun of the construct chain (yadā abī lahabin). The genitive is governed by the preceding muḍāf abī.

Noun, masculine singular, nominative (marfūʿ), definite by pronoun annexation (iḍāfa) — functioning as subject (fāʿil) of the verb aghnā. Root م و ل (m-w-l). The -hu suffix is a 3rd person masculine singular possessive pronoun. māl denotes any form of material wealth — money, property, livestock, goods. Syntactically delayed after the verb and prepositional phrase (aghnā ʿanhu), placing emphasis on the negation rather than the subject.

Indefinite noun in the accusative (direct object of sayaṣlā). The tanwīn (-an) marks indefiniteness. The choice of indefinite form (nāran rather than al-nāra) can indicate tafkhīm (magnification: a fire so immense it defies identification) or taḥqīr (classification: a particular type of fire).

Feminine singular of dhū (possessor/master), in the accusative case agreeing with nāran. Functions as a ṣifa (adjective) for nāran, creating an iḍāfa construction with lahabin. Grammatically: accusative feminine singular adjective in construct state.

Indefinite noun in the genitive case, governed by the iḍāfa construction with dhāta. The tanwīn with kasra (-in) marks genitive indefinite. Root l-h-b refers specifically to the visible, leaping tongue of fire — not fire as substance (nār) but fire as visible, dynamic activity.

Noun, concrete (ism), feminine, nominative (marfūʿ) — subject of the clause. The tāʾ marbūṭa marks feminine. The possessive pronoun -hū (his) creates an iḍāfa-like annexation: "woman-of-him." Nominative as subject coordinated with the implied subject of the preceding ayahs.

Intensive active participle (ism mubālagha) on the faʿʿāla pattern, feminine, accusative (manṣūb). The accusative case is the crux of grammatical debate: (1) ḥāl — circumstantial state describing imraʾatuhū, (2) badal — appositional substitute, (3) manṣūb ʿalā l-dhamm — accusative of censure (a special Arabic construction where accusative case itself enacts blame). The faʿʿāla pattern indicates habitual, intensive, professional action — not a one-time carrying but a defining occupation.

Noun, concrete (ism), masculine, genitive (majrūr) — in iḍāfa with ḥammālata. The definite article al- makes this SPECIFIC firewood — known, notorious, identified. Pattern: faʿal. The genitive is governed by the construct state (muḍāf ilayh).

Noun (ism), masculine singular, genitive (majrūr) governed by fī. The possessive pronoun -hā (her) is attached, referring to the woman described in 111:4 (ḥammālata l-ḥaṭab). jīd is specifically the front part of the neck, the part adorned with necklaces and displayed with pride — distinct from 'unuq (the general neck) or raqaba (the back of the neck / the neck as seat of bondage). This is a hapax legomenon in the Quran — it appears only here.

Noun (ism), masculine singular, indefinite (nakirah), nominative (marfūʿ) as the mubtadaʾ (subject) of the nominal sentence. The tanwīn (-un) marks indefiniteness — "a rope" not "the rope." The delayed position after the prepositional phrase fī jīdihā creates rhetorical suspense: the location is revealed before the object. The indefiniteness suggests either one of many ropes (non-specific), or an indeterminate, unknowable kind of rope (amplifying dread).

Noun (ism), masculine singular, indefinite (nakirah), genitive (majrūr) governed by min. The tanwīn marks indefiniteness. masad is a verbal noun or quasi-verbal noun from the root m-s-d, carrying the sense of "tightly twisted fiber." It is a hapax legomenon in the Quran — the root appears only here. The surah itself (al-Masad) takes its name from this word, underscoring its thematic centrality.

Proper noun (ism 'alam), definite, nominative (marfu'). Functions as mubtada' (subject) if huwa is damir al-sha'n, or as badal (appositive) if huwa is referential. The lam is assimilated (lam shamsiyya applied to the divine name). Carries the definite article al-, indicating uniqueness.

Indefinite numeral noun (ism 'adad), nominative (marfu'), with tanwin. Functions as khabar (predicate) of the nominal clause. The tanwin (-un) on ahadun is significant: it could indicate indefiniteness (generalizing — "a one") or tanwin al-ta'zim (tanwin of grandeur — "One" with emphasis). The choice of ahad over wahid is grammatically and theologically deliberate.
Proper noun, nominative (marfu'), functioning as mubtada' (subject) of a nominal sentence. The definite form with the assimilated lam (al-lah) is the proper divine name, distinct from ilah (a god).
Proper noun/adjective used as khabar (predicate) in the nominal sentence. Nominative (marfu'). The definite article al- marks it as THE samad, making it a title rather than a quality.
Noun (abstract), indefinite accusative (mansub with tanwin). Functions as copular predicate (khabar kana) in the negative existential clause. From root k-f-' meaning equality, equivalence, matching.
Noun (numeral), indefinite nominative (marfu' with tanwin). Delayed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar) of the negated copula yakun. In negative context, ahadun means "not one, no one, not anyone."
Prepositional phrase: PREP بِ (bāʾ al-istiʿāna / al-mulābasa) + NOUN رَبّ in genitive (majrūr) by iḍāfa with the following al-falaq; bi- binds the act of seeking refuge (aʿūdhu) to the protector
Noun, definite with al-, genitive as second element of iḍāfa (rabbi l-falaqi). From root f-l-q. The al- prefix indicates a known, specific entity — THE splitting, not any splitting.
Noun (ism) in the genitive case (majrūr) governed by min; head of an iḍāfa (genitive construct) with mā khalaqa as muḍāf ilayhi; indefinite in meaning though formally definite by annexation

Noun (ism), masculine, genitive (majrūr) governed by min. First term of an iḍāfa construct (muḍāf) with ghāsiqin as muḍāf ilayh. The form sharr is a maṣdar/abstract noun meaning "evil, harm." Note: MASAQ maps this to ش ر ي (sh-r-y) which includes both the "evil" semantic field (sharr) and the "buying/selling" field (shirā'/ishtarā). The "evil" meanings derive from the root ش ر ر (sh-r-r) in classical analysis, though MASAQ groups them under sh-r-y. Both root analyses are presented.

Active participle (ism fā'il) on the fa'il pattern, masculine singular, indefinite (with tanwīn), genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayh in the construct sharri ghāsiqin. The active participle indicates an ongoing agent: "one that is [currently/habitually] darkening." The indefiniteness (tanwīn) is significant — it does not specify WHICH darkening entity, preserving ambiguity between night, moon, any celestial body, or any abstract darkening force.

Noun (ism), genitive case (majrūr) governed by min. Indefinite in meaning but definite by iḍāfa — the sharr is specified by what follows (the naffāthāt). First element of an iḍāfa chain: sharru → n-naffāthāti (evil OF the blowers). Form: sharr, verbal noun / maṣdar-like noun from sh-r-r.

Intensive active participle (ism fāʿil mubālagha), pattern faʿʿālāt, feminine plural, genitive case (majrūr) as second element of iḍāfa with sharr. The doubling of the fāʾ (naffāthāt vs nāfithāt) indicates intensity, habitual action, or professional engagement. Definite with al-.

Noun (ism), plural of ʿuqda, genitive case (majrūr) governed by fī. Definite with al-. Pattern: fuʿal, broken plural. The root ʿ-q-d conveys tying, binding, contracting, making firm. Syntactically serves as PREP_OBJ (object of preposition fī).

Noun (ism), genitive case (majrūr) governed by مِن. In genitive construct (iḍāfa) with حَاسِدٍ — "evil of an envier." The root sh-r-r (NOT sh-r-y as MASAQ suggests) carries the sense of evil, harm, badness. MASAQ assigns root ش ر ي which includes "to buy/sell" — but شَرّ (sharr) "evil" is from ش ر ر (sh-r-r), a geminate root.

Active participle (ism fāʿil) from Form I فَاعِل (fāʿil) pattern. Indefinite (nakira), genitive case (majrūr) as second term of iḍāfa with شَرِّ. The active participle indicates an ongoing characteristic — this is someone whose nature/habit is envy, not merely someone who envied once.

Preposition بِ (ḥarf jarr) governing genitive — in istiʿādha context marks the entity sought for refuge (instrument/adhesion) — + noun رَبّ masculine singular genitive (majrūr) governed by bi-, first term of an iḍāfa with al-nāsi ("the Lord of mankind"); the genitive case is doubly motivated by bi- and by the iḍāfa structure; rabb functions as a ṣifa mushabbaha or verbal noun from r-b-b serving as a divine title

Noun (ism), masculine singular (collective noun functioning as generic plural), genitive (majrūr) as the second term of the idafa rabbi l-nasi. The definite article al- marks the generic category — ALL of humankind, not a specific group. The form al-nas is a shortened form of al-unas (the sociable beings), with the initial hamza and vowel elided.
Noun, genitive (majrur), in apposition to rabb in 114:1. First element of idafa with al-nas. Pattern fa'il (CaCiC) denoting agent/doer.
Noun, definite with al-, genitive (majrur) as second element of idafa with malik. Concrete noun denoting the entirety of humankind.

Noun, concrete, genitive case (kasra), in apposition (badal or 'atf bayan) to rabb in 114:1. First element of genitive construct (idafa) with al-nas. Indefinite form (no al-) entering construct state.
Noun, concrete, definite (al-), genitive case (kasra), second element of genitive construct (mudaf ilayh) with ilahi. Governed in genitive by the construct state.

Abstract noun (maṣdar/ism), masculine, genitive (majrūr) governed by min. Functions as muḍāf in the construct sharri l-waswāsi, making al-waswās the muḍāf ilayh. The MASAQ assigns root ش ر ي (sh-r-y) which covers both the "evil/harm" semantic field and the "purchase/sell" field. The form sharr (without final yāʾ) belongs specifically to the "evil" semantic domain, classically traced to ش ر ر (sh-r-r) by many lexicographers.

Noun (fa'lāl pattern — verbal noun or intensive agent noun), masculine, genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayh in the construct sharri l-waswāsi. The definite article al- marks it as a known, specific entity. The quadriliteral root w-s-w-s is formed by reduplication of the bilateral w-s, and the pattern waswās can function as either a maṣdar (the act of whispering) or an agent noun (the one who whispers). This dual function is grammatically unresolved and semantically productive.

Intensive adjective (ṣīghat al-mubālagha), fa''āl pattern (فَعَّال), masculine, genitive (majrūr) as apposition (badal) or attributive adjective (naʿt) to al-waswāsi. The fa''āl pattern denotes habitual, repeated action — not one who withdrew once but one who CONSTANTLY withdraws. This is the second epithet in the dual characterization of the entity, specifying its mode of operation: withdrawal after approach.
Noun, broken plural of sadr, genitive case (governed by fi). Second element in genitive chain with al-nas. The plural universalizes: ALL chests of ALL mankind.
Noun, definite with al-, genitive case (second element of idafa with sudur). The definite article al- universalizes: THE people = ALL people, not a subset.
Definite noun, genitive case (governed by min). Collective noun referring to the jinn as a class. The tashdiid on the nun indicates the geminate root j-n-n.
Definite noun, genitive case (governed by min via conjunction with al-jinnati). Generic article — refers to the entire human species.
